definition_zh: 各种各样的；不同的、好几个的；多方面的
definition_en: of several different kinds or several different people or things
core_image: 一排货架上摆着颜色形状各不相同的盒子，标签却写着同一类商品
scene: 聚会结束后，桌上留下了各色各样的杯子，高矮粗细都不相同。Various guests arrived through the evening, each with a different story.
sceneCN: 这里 various 是「各种各样的」（第 1 个义项：种类不止一种）；句意为整晚陆续来了各种各样的客人，每人都有不同的故事。一排彼此不同的盒子，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：各种各样的；不同的、好几个的；多方面的

derivatives.zh: 副词，义为「以各种方式、不同地」
名词，义为「多样性、种类」，是本词的名词形式
动词，义为「变化、不同」
名词，义为「多样性」，较少使用
形容词，义为「多样的、各不相同的」

senses.title: Of several kinds
senses.titleCN: 各种各样的：种类不止一个
senses.definition: of more than one kind, used before a plural noun
senses.definitionCN: 不止一种，用在复数名词前
senses.example: Various guests arrived through the evening, each with a different story.
senses.exampleCN: 整晚陆续来了各种各样的客人，每人都有不同的故事。
senses.why: Latin varius means spotted or mixed; various names a set whose members do not match.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 varius 意为斑驳的、混杂的；various 指成员彼此不一致的一组。

senses.title: Several and different
senses.titleCN: 好几个不同的：数量不定但都算在内
senses.definition: several different people or things, not exactly numbered
senses.definitionCN: 几个不同的人或物，数量不确切
senses.example: We met at various times during the year.
senses.exampleCN: 我们这一年里在不同时间见过几次。
senses.why: The word avoids giving a number; it counts only as far as several and no further.
senses.whyCN: 这个词回避给出具体数目：只数到「好几个」为止。

senses.title: From many sides
senses.titleCN: 多方面的：原因、来源各不相同
senses.definition: coming from many different sources or aspects
senses.definitionCN: 来自许多不同来源或方面
senses.example: The delay was due to various reasons, some of them personal.
senses.exampleCN: 延误有种种原因，其中一些是私人的。
senses.why: Each member of the set has its own origin; the word holds them side by side.
senses.whyCN: 这一组的每个成员各有来源，这个词把它们并排放着。

senses.title: Many-sided in skill
senses.titleCN: 多样化的：本事不止一样（较少用）
senses.definition: having many different abilities or forms, in older or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 具有多种才能或形态，较旧的文学用法
senses.example: He is a various man, at home in both music and mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个多才之人，音乐和数学都能应付。
senses.why: The older sense applies the diversity to a single person, not to a group.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的含义把多样性用在一个人身上，而不是一群人身上。

intro.en: Various is the English form of Latin varius, spotted or mixed, with an adjective ending added on the way.
intro.cn: various 是拉丁语 varius「斑驳的、混杂的」在英语里的形态，途中加上了形容词词尾。

items.en: The adjective varius described things of mixed colour, uneven or of several kinds.
items.cn: 形容词 varius 描述颜色混杂、不齐整或多种多样的事物。

items.en: Its plural varii was used for several different people, close to the modern sense.
items.cn: 其复数 varii 用于指若干不同的人，很接近现代含义。

items.en: English formed various from the Latin stem, first meaning changeable or diverse.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁词干造出 various，最初意为易变的或多样的。

items.en: Modern usage settles it before plural nouns, meaning several different.
items.cn: 现代用法把它固定在复数名词前，表示好几个不同的。

items.en: The word now shares its family with variety, variable and vary, all from the same Latin stem.
items.cn: 它如今与 variety、variable、vary 共用一个家族，全部出自同一拉丁词干。

note.en: The look-alike group is the vari- family; the near-meaning group holds quantifiers for a loose plurality.
note.cn: 形近组是 vari- 家族；近义组收表示不确切多数的限定词。

entries.definition: The noun for many kinds or one kind.
The verb, to differ or change.
Made varied, not all alike; close to various in sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多样的」，意义接近 various。

entries.definition: Able to change, or a symbol that varies.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」。

entries.definition: More than two but not many, without the sense of unlike.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，义为「几个」，不强调彼此不同。

entries.definition: Not the same as one another, the core of various.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不同的」，是 various 的核心义。

entries.definition: Of mixed kinds put together, often in a box or pack.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「什锦的、搭配好的」。

entries.definition: Many in number, with no emphasis on variety.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「众多的」，不强调种类。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the prefix habit of various and real collocations such as for various reasons.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子利用 various 只修饰复数的习惯，以及 for various reasons 这类真实搭配。

normal.en: Various always sits before a plural noun: various reasons, never various reason.
normal.cn: various 总在复数名词前：various reasons，不能接单数。

normal.en: Various means more than one, but it refuses to say how many.
normal.cn: various 表示不止一个，却不肯说有几个。

normal.en: For various reasons is a polite way to avoid listing the reasons.
normal.cn: for various reasons 是避免一一列举的礼貌说法。

normal.en: Varied describes a thing, various describes a group of things.
normal.cn: varied 形容一样东西，various 形容一组东西。

normal.en: The same root gives variety, vary and variable.
normal.cn: 同一个词根还给出 variety、vary 与 variable。

abstract.en: Various is a quiet way of saying that a group refuses to be summed up in one word.
abstract.cn: various 是一个低调的说法：这一组无法用一个词概括。

abstract.en: The word is plural by nature; it draws its meaning from the gaps between members.
abstract.cn: 这个词天生带复数性：它的意思来自成员之间的差异。

abstract.en: Say various and you admit you have not checked everything, only that the pieces differ.
abstract.cn: 说 various 就等于承认你并未逐一核对，只确认了它们互不相同。

examples.en: Various people offered to help with the move.
examples.cn: 有好几个人主动提出帮忙搬家。

examples.en: The delay was caused by various problems with the engine.
examples.cn: 延误差是由发动机的种种问题造成的。

examples.en: Books on the subject are available in various languages.
examples.cn: 这个主题的书有各种语言的版本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我瑞爱死」——各式各样的东西我瑞（锐）意爱死：各种各样的

root: 源自拉丁语形容词 varius「斑驳的、多种的」，经英语自造词 various 进入使用；同族词有 variety、vary、variation、variable。

sensesIntro.en: Various ranges from many kinds before a plural noun, to an unnumbered several, many sources, and an older sense of many-sided.
sensesIntro.cn: various 从复数名词前的「多种」，到不确切的好几个、多来源，以及较旧的「多才」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shelf of boxes, same category, every shape and colour different.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排货架上的盒子同属一类，却个个形状颜色不同。

branches.en: KIND LINE: the members are not alike.
branches.cn: 种类线：成员彼此并不相同。

branches.en: COUNT LINE: several, with no exact number.
branches.cn: 计数线：好几个，不给具体数字。

branches.en: ORIGIN LINE: causes and sources differ.
branches.cn: 来源线：原因与出处各异。

branches.en: ABILITY LINE: one person with many sides.
branches.cn: 才能线：一个人有多面。

branches.en: CONTRAST: various refuses both one word and a fixed number.
branches.cn: 对照线：various 既不肯概括，也不肯给数。

intro.en: Various is a Latin stem with an English adjective ending; the whole vari- family shares the stem.
intro.cn: various 是拉丁词干加英语形容词词尾，整个 vari- 家族共用该词干。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is varius; the plural varii already meant several different people.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 varius，其复数 varii 已经表示「若干不同的人」。

definition_zh: 变化；变动；使不同；各不相同；（随情况）改变
definition_en: to change, or to differ from one another
core_image: 同一把尺子量十个人，每量一次读数都不一样
scene: 山脚下是春天的花，爬到半山就只见残雪，山顶则冻得人发抖。Prices vary from shop to shop along the same street.
sceneCN: 这里 vary 是「各不相同、有差异」（第 2 个义项：彼此不同）；句意为同一条街上各家店铺的价格各不相同。尺子每次读数都不一样，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：变化、变动；使不同；各不相同

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「多样性、种类」
形容词，义为「各种各样的」
形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」
名词，义为「变化、差异」
形容词，义为「多样的、各不相同的」

senses.title: To change over time
senses.definition: to change in amount, level or form over time
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、水平或形式上随时间改变
senses.example: The water level varies with the season.
senses.exampleCN: 水位随季节变化。
senses.why: Latin variare means to make different; the verb follows whatever the changing thing does.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 variare 意为使不同；这个动词跟着变化者一起走。

senses.title: To differ from one another
senses.definition: to be different between individual cases
senses.definitionCN: 在各个个体之间有所不同
senses.example: Prices vary from shop to shop along the same street.
senses.exampleCN: 同一条街上各家店铺的价格各不相同。
senses.why: Here nothing changes over time; the differences exist side by side in one moment.
senses.whyCN: 这里没有随时间而变化，差别在同一时刻并排存在。

senses.title: To change deliberately
senses.titleCN: 主动改变：故意换个做法
senses.definition: to make something different on purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有意使某物不同
senses.example: He never varies his route to work.
senses.exampleCN: 他上班路线从不改变。
senses.why: The subject is a person here, and the change is a choice rather than a natural drift.
senses.whyCN: 这里的主语是人，变化是一种选择而不是自然漂移。

senses.title: To depend on something
senses.titleCN: 随……而变：跟着另一个因素走
senses.definition: to change according to another factor
senses.definitionCN: 随另一个因素改变
senses.example: Crop yields vary according to rainfall and soil.
senses.exampleCN: 作物产量随降雨与土壤而变化。
senses.why: The verb leaves the subject to someone else: yields follow the rain, and the rain decides.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把主导权交给别人：产量跟着雨水走，由雨水决定。

intro.en: Vary is the direct Latin verb variare, to make different, taken into English without an ending change.
intro.cn: vary 就是拉丁语动词 variare「使不同」几乎原样进入英语。

items.en: The adjective varius meant spotted, mixed or of several kinds.
items.cn: 形容词 varius 意为斑驳的、混杂的、多种多样的。

items.en: The verb variare meant to make different, to alternate or to diversify.
items.cn: 动词 variare 意为使不同、交替变换、使多样化。

items.en: Old French variier softened the Latin verb and gave it a French shape.
items.cn: 古法语 variier 让拉丁动词软化，并赋予它法语形态。

items.en: English shortened it to vary in the fourteenth century, meaning to undergo change.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪把它缩短为 vary，意为经历变化。

items.en: Modern English uses it both for changing and for differing, two sides of one Latin idea.
items.cn: 现代英语既用它表「变化」也表「不同」，这是同一个拉丁观念的两面。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the vari- family; the near-meaning group holds verbs of shifting and differing.
note.cn: 形近组沿 vari- 家族；近义组收表示变化与不同的动词。

entries.definition: Of many kinds, the adjective of the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「各种各样的」，同词干。

entries.definition: Many kinds or one kind; the noun of the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「多样性、种类」，同词干。

entries.definition: Something that changes, or a symbol for it.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或名词，义为「可变的、变量」。

entries.definition: A change or difference in amount or form.
The plain verb for becoming different.
To be unlike, only the side of comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「不同」，只表示比较的一面。

entries.definition: To rise and fall again and again, like a level.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「波动」，反复起落。

entries.definition: To move from one position or state to another.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「转移」，从一个位置或状态移到另一个。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the two faces of vary, changing and differing, with real phrases from news and shops.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用 vary 变化与不同这两面，搭配取自新闻与店铺的真实说法。

normal.en: Vary with time, differ from place to place: one word for both.
normal.cn: 随时间变叫 vary，各地不同也叫 vary：一个词两面用。

normal.en: Prices vary widely means the range is large.
normal.cn: prices vary widely 指差价范围很大。

normal.en: Vary in size means the sizes are not all the same.
normal.cn: vary in size 指大小并不一样。

normal.en: Opinions vary is a polite way of saying nobody agrees.
normal.cn: opinions vary 是「谁都不一致」的礼貌说法。

normal.en: Varied is the adjective, variety the noun, varying the participle.
normal.cn: varied 是形容词，variety 是名词，varying 是分词。

abstract.en: Vary needs two reference points: a thing at two times, or two things at one time.
abstract.cn: vary 需要两个参照点：一样东西的两个时刻，或同一时刻的两样东西。

abstract.en: Change is motion, difference is structure; vary describes both with one shape.
abstract.cn: 变化是运动，差异是结构；vary 用一个形状描述两者。

abstract.en: A life without vary is a line, not a landscape.
abstract.cn: 没有变化的生活是一条线，不是一片风景。

examples.en: Prices vary widely between the two markets.
examples.cn: 两个市场的价格差别很大。

examples.en: Her mood varies with the weather.
examples.cn: 她的心情随天气变化。

examples.en: The recipes vary only in the amount of sugar used.
examples.cn: 这些食谱只是在用糖量上不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威瑞」——威（风）瑞（雨）一来，天气就变：变化

root: 直接来自拉丁语动词 variare「使不同、变换」，经古法语 variier 于十四世纪进入英语；同族词有 various、variety、variable、variation。

sensesIntro.en: Vary covers change over time, difference between cases, deliberate change and dependence on a factor.
sensesIntro.cn: vary 涵盖随时间变化、个体间差异、主动改变与随因素而变四种情形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one ruler measuring ten people, with ten different readings.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子量十个人，十次读数都不同。

branches.en: TIME LINE: the same thing is different later.
branches.cn: 时间线：同一样东西后来不同了。

branches.en: SPACE LINE: different cases at one moment.
branches.cn: 空间线：同一时刻的各个个体不同。

branches.en: WILL LINE: a person chooses to change.
branches.cn: 意志线：人主动选择改变。

branches.en: CAUSE LINE: one factor pulls another along.
branches.cn: 因果线：一个因素带着另一个走。

branches.en: CONTRAST: change is one thing twice, vary also covers two things once.
branches.cn: 对照线：变化是一样东西的两次，vary 也含两样东西的一次。

intro.en: Vary is a bare Latin verb stem; its English relatives come from adding endings to the same root.
intro.cn: vary 是不带前缀的拉丁动词词干，英语亲属词都在同一词根上加词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is variare from varius; the English verb drops the ending entirely.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是出自 varius 的 variare，英语动词整个去掉了词尾。

items.example: It forms varied and the past tense.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 varied 与过去式。

items.example: It is shared by the whole family.

definition_zh: 巨大的；广阔的；浩瀚的；大量的、极多的
definition_en: extremely large in area, amount or degree
core_image: 站在沙丘顶端望出去，地平线一直退到眼睛看不见的地方
scene: 夜里没有一盏灯，抬头只看见铺满星星的天。A vast plain stretched away in every direction.
sceneCN: 这里 vast 是「广阔的、浩瀚的」（第 1 个义项：面积极大）；句意为一片广阔的平原向四面八方伸展开去。地平线退到看不见的地方，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：巨大的、广阔的、浩瀚的；大量的

derivatives.zh: 副词，义为「极大地、远远地」，如 vastly improved
名词，义为「广阔、浩瀚」
名词，书面说法，义为「广袤」，较少使用

senses.title: Enormous in area
senses.titleCN: 面积巨大：眼睛望不到边
senses.definition: extremely large in area or extent
senses.definitionCN: 面积或范围极大
senses.example: A vast plain stretched away in every direction.
senses.exampleCN: 一片广阔的平原向四面八方伸展开去。
senses.why: Latin vastus meant empty and desolate; the emptiness itself is what takes the breath away.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vastus 意为空旷荒芜；正是这种空旷让人屏息。

senses.title: Enormous in amount
senses.titleCN: 数量巨大：多到难以清点
senses.definition: extremely large in number or quantity
senses.definitionCN: 数量或数目极大
senses.example: A vast amount of data was collected over ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 十年间收集了海量的数据。
senses.why: The word moves from space to quantity: numbers can also open out like a plain.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从空间移到数量：数字也能像平原一样铺开。

senses.title: Great in degree
senses.titleCN: 程度巨大：差别或优势悬殊
senses.definition: very great in degree, used of differences and advantages
senses.definitionCN: 在程度上非常大，用于差别与优势
senses.example: There is a vast difference between the two plans.
senses.exampleCN: 两个方案之间差别巨大。
senses.why: Here the size is abstract: not metres but distance in quality or outcome.
senses.whyCN: 这里的大小是抽象的：量的是质量或结果上的距离，而非米数。

senses.title: The great majority
senses.titleCN: 绝大多数：人群中的绝大部分
senses.definition: used with majority to mean almost all
senses.definitionCN: 与 majority 连用，表示几乎全部
senses.example: The vast majority of students passed the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 绝大多数学生通过了考试。
senses.why: A crowd can be vast too; the same word measures people.
senses.whyCN: 人群也可以是 vast；同一个词也能量人。

intro.en: Vast comes from Latin vastus, empty and desolate, which already described land that stretched out bare.
intro.cn: vast 来自拉丁语 vastus「空旷荒芜的」，本已形容光秃秃铺展开的土地。

items.en: The adjective vastus meant empty, waste or desolate, applied to ruined land.
items.cn: 形容词 vastus 意为空旷的、荒废的、荒凉的，用于被毁坏的土地。

items.en: Its verb vastare meant to lay waste, and lies behind English waste and devastate.
items.cn: 其动词 vastare 意为摧残荒废，是英语 waste 与 devastate 的来源。

items.en: Old French vaste kept the sense of wide and unoccupied space.
items.cn: 古法语 vaste 保留了辽阔空旷的意思。

items.en: English borrowed vast in the fifteenth century for enormous extent.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 vast，表示范围极大。

items.en: Modern usage extends it from land to amounts and differences, while the sense of emptiness fades.
items.cn: 现代用法把它从土地扩展到数量与差别，同时「空旷」的感觉渐渐淡去。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin stem of waste and emptiness; the near-meaning group holds words for great size.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示「荒废、空」的拉丁词干；近义组收表示巨大的词。

entries.definition: By a very large amount; the adverb.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「极大地」，是本词的副词形式。

entries.definition: The quality of being vast; the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「广阔」，是本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: To lay waste or ruin; uses the Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「毁坏」，出自同一拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Empty or unused land; a distant English cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「荒地、浪费」，英语里的远亲。

entries.definition: Very large in size, plainer and more everyday.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「巨大的」，更日常。

entries.definition: So large it cannot be measured; close in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无边的」，语气接近。

entries.definition: Larger than normal, with a hint of shock.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「庞大的」，带惊奇感。

entries.definition: Having no limits, stressing no edge rather than size.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无边无际的」，强调没有边界。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the empty-plain core and real collocations like vast majority.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「空旷平原」意象与 vast majority 这类真实搭配。

normal.en: Vast majority means almost all, not merely most.
normal.cn: vast majority 指几乎全部，不只是大多数。

normal.en: Vast came from a Latin word for empty land.
normal.cn: vast 来自拉丁语中表示空地的词。

normal.en: Vast difference is a huge gap, not a big object.
normal.cn: vast difference 指巨大差距，不是巨大物件。

normal.en: Vaster and vastest exist, though writers often use more vast.
normal.cn: vaster 与 vastest 存在，但作家常用 more vast。

normal.en: Vastly improved means improved by a very large amount.
normal.cn: vastly improved 指改善幅度极大。

abstract.en: Vast began as emptiness and became size: the feeling of distance is older than the measure of it.
abstract.cn: vast 从「空」长成「大」：对距离的感受比测量更古老。

abstract.en: Something vast makes the viewer small, which is why the word always carries a trace of awe.
abstract.cn: 巨大之物让人显小，所以这个词总带一丝敬畏。

abstract.en: The same word measures land, data and differences, because largeness is a comparison, not a substance.
abstract.cn: 同一个词量土地、数据与差别，因为「大」是比较，不是实体。

examples.en: Vast areas of the country remain uninhabited.
examples.cn: 这个国家的大片地区仍无人居住。

examples.en: She spent a vast amount of time on the research.
examples.cn: 她在这项研究上花了大量时间。

examples.en: The vast majority of customers were satisfied.
examples.cn: 绝大多数顾客表示满意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哇死他」——哇，他一个人管那么大一片地：广阔的

root: 源自拉丁语形容词 vastus「空旷荒芜的」及其动词 vastare「荒废」，经古法语 vaste 于十五世纪进入英语；同族词有 devastate、waste。

sensesIntro.en: Vast starts with land that has no edge, then measures quantities, differences and the bulk of a crowd.
sensesIntro.cn: vast 从望不到边的土地开始，然后用来量数量、差别与人群的绝大部分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a horizon that keeps moving back as you look at it.
core.cn: 核心意象：你越看，那条地平线退得越远。

branches.en: SPACE LINE: land and water without visible edge.
branches.cn: 空间线：看不见边际的陆地与水面。

branches.en: QUANTITY LINE: numbers or data in huge bulk.
branches.cn: 数量线：成堆的数字与数据。

branches.en: DEGREE LINE: a gap that feels like distance.
branches.cn: 程度线：像距离一样的悬殊。

branches.en: CROWD LINE: nearly all the people counted.
branches.cn: 人群线：被计数的人几乎全部。

branches.en: CONTRAST: huge is a size, vast is a stretch.
branches.cn: 对照线：huge 指尺寸，vast 指铺展。

intro.en: Vast is a whole Latin stem; its English relatives take -ly and -ness, while devastate keeps the Latin verb.
intro.cn: vast 是完整的拉丁词干，英语亲属词接 -ly 与 -ness，而 devastate 保留拉丁动词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pair is the adjective vastus and the verb vastare, both about emptiness and ruin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的一对是形容词 vastus 与动词 vastare，都与空旷和毁坏有关。

items.example: It shows the old root in English.
items.exampleCN: 它在英语里展示这个老词根。

definition_zh: 蔬菜；植物（总称，较旧用法）；形容词：植物的、蔬菜的；植物人（口语，多用于 be a vegetable）
definition_en: a plant or part of a plant eaten as food, such as a carrot or cabbage
core_image: 菜篮里横着一根带泥的胡萝卜，叶子还挂着水珠
scene: 厨房案板上摊着刚洗好的青菜、辣椒和番茄，水还在滴。She grows most of her own vegetables in a small garden.
sceneCN: 这里 vegetable 是「蔬菜」（第 1 个义项：可食用的植物或其部分）；句意为她大部分的蔬菜都种在自己的小园子里。菜篮里那根带泥的胡萝卜，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「素食者」，由本词加 -arian 构成
名词，义为「植被、草木」，同源于拉丁语 vegetare「生长」
动词，义为「生长；无所事事地过日子」
形容词，义为「植物的」，较书面

senses.title: Food from plants
senses.titleCN: 蔬菜：可吃的植物或其部分
senses.definition: a plant or part of a plant used as food, such as cabbage or carrot
senses.definitionCN: 可食用的植物或其部分，如甘蓝、胡萝卜
senses.example: She grows most of her own vegetables in a small garden.
senses.exampleCN: 她大部分的蔬菜都种在自己的小园子里。
senses.why: Latin vegetare means to grow; a vegetable is simply the part of a growing plant that reaches the table.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vegetare 意为生长；蔬菜就是生长中的植物里走上餐桌的那一部分。

senses.title: Plants in general
senses.titleCN: 植物：较旧的总称，常带科学色彩
senses.definition: a plant or plant life in general, in older or scientific writing
senses.definitionCN: 笼统指植物，见于较早或科学性的文字
senses.example: The museum has a large collection of fossils of ancient vegetables.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆收藏了大量古代植物的化石。
senses.why: The older sense covers the whole kingdom; the kitchen sense pulled one part of it away.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的含义覆盖整个界，厨房用法把其中一部分拽了出来。

senses.title: Of plants
senses.titleCN: 植物的：作定语说明来源
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean made from or of plants
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，表示由植物制成或与植物有关
senses.example: The soup was cooked in vegetable oil rather than butter.
senses.exampleCN: 汤是用植物油而不是黄油煮的。
senses.why: As a modifier the word labels a source, not a kind of plant.
senses.whyCN: 作修饰语时，这个词标的是来源，而不是某种植物。

senses.title: A person without response
senses.titleCN: 植物人：口语里形容毫无反应的人
senses.definition: in informal medical talk, a person alive but unable to respond or move
senses.definitionCN: 口语医疗说法，指活着却无法回应或活动的人
senses.example: He was no longer ill, but he lay as a vegetable for years.
senses.exampleCN: 他的病已不是问题，却像植物人一样躺了多年。
senses.why: The metaphor is blunt: only growth remains, all communication gone.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻很直接：只剩生长，一切交流都消失了。

intro.en: Vegetable comes from Latin vegetabilis, able to grow, from the verb vegetare, to be lively.
intro.cn: vegetable 来自拉丁语 vegetabilis「能生长的」，出自动词 vegetare「有生气、生长」。

items.en: The verb vegere meant to be active or lively, applied to anything growing and powered.
items.cn: 动词 vegere 意为有活力、活跃，用于正在生长、有生机的东西。

items.en: Its frequentative vegetare meant to animate or make grow, the root of the whole family.
items.cn: 其反复态 vegetare 意为使有生气、使生长，是整个词族的根。

items.en: The adjective vegetabilis meant capable of growth, applied to plants and soil.
items.cn: 形容词 vegetabilis 意为能生长的，用于植物与土壤。

items.en: Old French used vegetable for anything that grew, and English borrowed it in that sense.
items.cn: 古法语用 vegetable 指一切会生长之物，英语即以此义借入。

items.en: By the eighteenth century the kitchen sense had pushed the general one aside in daily speech.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，厨房里的用法在日常语言中把笼统的含义挤到了一边。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the grow- family; the near-meaning group holds plant foods and words for plants.
note.cn: 形近组沿「生长」词族；近义组收植物性食物与泛指植物的词。

entries.definition: A person who avoids meat; built on vegetable.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「素食者」，由本词构成。

entries.definition: Plant life as a whole, the old general sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「植被」，即较旧的笼统含义。

entries.definition: To grow as a plant, or to live without activity.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「生长」，也指无所事事地活着。

entries.definition: A learned adjective for plant life.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「植物的」，书面色彩。

entries.definition: One common vegetable, with its own round picture.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「卷心菜」，单一蔬菜，画面自成一格。

entries.definition: The seed-bearing part, a kitchen partner and rival.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「水果」，含籽的部分，厨房里的伙伴与对手。

entries.definition: Farm products sold together, fruit and vegetables at once.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「农产品」，把果蔬一起算。

entries.definition: Plants grown for harvest, seen as a field or yield.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「作物」，从田野与产量的角度看。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the growing-plant root and the kitchen sense that now dominates.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「生长植物」的词根，以及如今占主导的厨房含义。

normal.en: Vegetable comes from a Latin verb meaning to grow.
normal.cn: vegetable 出自一个意为「生长」的拉丁动词。

normal.en: Vegetables are eaten; a vegetarian eats no meat.
normal.cn: 蔬菜是吃的，而 vegetarian 是不吃肉的人。

normal.en: Vegetation is the old, wide sense: all of the plants.
normal.cn: vegetation 是旧的宽泛指：所有植物。

normal.en: Vegetable oil is oil pressed from plants, not from butter.
normal.cn: vegetable oil 是从植物压榨的油，不是黄油。

normal.en: A vegetable garden grows food, a flower garden grows beauty.
normal.cn: 菜园种食物，花园种美。

abstract.en: The word once meant anything that grows, and now means what we pick and cook.
abstract.cn: 这个词原指一切会生长之物，如今指我们采摘下锅的东西。

abstract.en: It marks a boundary humans drew, not one nature keeps: tomato is a fruit in botany and a vegetable in the kitchen.
abstract.cn: 它标的是人划的界线而非自然的：番茄在植物学是果实，在厨房是蔬菜。

abstract.en: From life to food to mere survival, the same root covers growth, harvest and the loss of speech.
abstract.cn: 从生命到食物再到只剩生存，同一个词根覆盖成长、收获与失语。

examples.en: Eat more fresh vegetables and less fried food.
examples.cn: 多吃新鲜蔬菜，少吃油炸食物。

examples.en: They planted vegetables behind the house.
examples.cn: 他们在屋后种了蔬菜。

examples.en: The dish is cooked with vegetable oil and garlic.
examples.cn: 这道菜用植物油和大蒜烹制。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威治特波」——威（为）治特（吃）吧，多吃蔬菜：蔬菜

root: 源自拉丁语 vegetabilis「能生长的」，出自 vegetare「使生长」，经古法语 vegetable 进入英语；同族词有 vegetarian、vegetation、vegetate。

sensesIntro.en: Vegetable moves from the whole plant kingdom to the kitchen, then to a modifier and an old blunt figure of speech.
sensesIntro.cn: vegetable 从整个植物界走进厨房，再成为修饰语，最后化作一句直白的旧比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a muddy carrot from the garden, leaves still beaded with water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根带泥的胡萝卜，叶子还挂着水珠。

branches.en: KITCHEN LINE: the edible part of a plant.
branches.cn: 厨房线：植物可食的部分。

branches.en: BOTANY LINE: the whole plant world, an older use.
branches.cn: 植物学线：整个植物界，较旧用法。

branches.en: LABEL LINE: vegetable oil names a source.
branches.cn: 标签线：vegetable oil 标的是来源。

branches.en: LOSS LINE: life without response, a blunt metaphor.
branches.cn: 丧失线：只剩生命而无反应，直白比喻。

branches.en: CONTRAST: a vegetable is food, vegetable oil is a material.
branches.cn: 对照线：vegetable 是食物，vegetable oil 是原料。

intro.en: Vegetable keeps its Latin adjective ending; English relatives use -arian, -ation and -ate.
intro.cn: vegetable 保留了拉丁形容词词尾，英语亲属词则用 -arian、-ation、-ate。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is vegere, vegetare and vegetabilis, all about life and growth.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁链条是 vegere、vegetare、vegetabilis，都与生命和生长有关。

items.example: It shows the word as a modifier.

definition_zh: 车辆；交通工具；（思想、信息的）传播媒介、手段；载体
definition_en: a machine with wheels or an engine used for transport, or a means of expressing something
core_image: 一辆车停在站台边，门一开，车上的人和想法一起下车
scene: 早高峰的马路上一排车缓缓挪动，尾灯连成一条红线。No vehicle is allowed on this narrow path.
sceneCN: 这里 vehicle 是「车辆」（第 1 个义项：有轮或有发动机的运输工具）；句意为这条窄路上不允许车辆通行。站台边停着的那辆车，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：车辆、交通工具；传播媒介、手段；载体

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「车辆的、车辆使用的」
名词短语，义为「车辆交通」

senses.title: A machine for transport
senses.titleCN: 车辆：能载人载货的机器
senses.definition: a machine with wheels or an engine used to carry people or goods
senses.definitionCN: 有轮或发动机、用来载人或载货的机器
senses.example: No vehicle is allowed on this narrow path.
senses.exampleCN: 这条窄路上不允许车辆通行。
senses.why: Latin vehiculum named a plain means of carrying, and the road sense grew from it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vehiculum 原指一种朴素的「搬运手段」，道路上的含义由此长出来。

senses.title: A means of expression
senses.titleCN: 表达手段：让思想能走动的载体
senses.definition: a way or medium through which ideas or feelings are expressed
senses.definitionCN: 使思想或感情得以表达的方式或媒介
senses.example: The novel served as a vehicle for her views on education.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说成了她表达教育观点的载体。
senses.why: What carries goods also carries ideas; the word moves from wheels to words.
senses.whyCN: 能载货的东西也能载思想；这个词从车轮走到了文字。

senses.title: A medium of transmission
senses.titleCN: 传播媒介：把信息或物质送到别处
senses.definition: a substance or channel that carries something to another place
senses.definitionCN: 把某物带到别处的物质或渠道
senses.example: Water is a common vehicle for disease in crowded cities.
senses.exampleCN: 在拥挤的城市里，水常是疾病的传播媒介。
senses.why: The word is neutral about what is carried: people, ideas or germs.
senses.whyCN: 这个词对载着什么保持中立：可以是人、思想或病菌。

senses.title: A medium in art and science
senses.titleCN: 溶剂、调色媒介：科学艺术里承载别物的东西
senses.definition: a liquid in which a substance is carried, as in paint or medicine
senses.definitionCN: 承载其他物质的液体，如颜料或药物里的媒介
senses.example: The pigments are held in an oil vehicle before the paint dries.
senses.exampleCN: 颜料在干之前由油性媒介承载。
senses.why: In a workshop the word returns to its plainest sense: something liquid does the carrying.
senses.whyCN: 在作坊里，这个词回到最朴素的意思：由一种液体来承担搬运。

intro.en: Vehicle comes from Latin vehiculum, a means of carrying, built from the verb vehere, to carry.
intro.cn: vehicle 来自拉丁语 vehiculum「搬运手段」，出自动词 vehere「运载」。

items.en: The verb vehere meant to carry or convey, said of riders, ships and carts.
items.cn: 动词 vehere 意为运载，用于骑手、船只和车。

items.en: Its noun vehiculum named any means of transport, not only a machine.
items.cn: 其名词 vehiculum 指任何运输手段，不只是机器。

items.en: French kept véhicule for carts and carriages, and English borrowed that sense.
items.cn: 法语保留 véhicule 指车马，英语借入的就是这一含义。

items.en: With the motor car the street sense tightened into vehicles on wheels.
items.cn: 随着汽车出现，日常含义收窄为带轮子的车辆。

items.en: At the same time the older sense of a carrier widened again into ideas and media.
items.cn: 与此同时，「承载物」的旧义又扩展开来，用于思想与媒介。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the veh- carrying stem; the near-meaning group holds transport words and carriers.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示「运载」的 veh- 词干；近义组收交通与承载相关的词。

entries.definition: Of or for vehicles; the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「车辆的」，是本词的形容词形式。

entries.definition: A blood vessel; sounds close but shares no root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「血管」，音近但不同根。

entries.definition: To carry something across; formed with con-.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「运送、传达」，同一拉丁词根加 con-。

entries.definition: A journey by sea; from the same carrying verb.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「航行」，出自同一个运载动词。

entries.definition: A passenger road vehicle, the everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「小汽车」，最日常的说法。

entries.definition: The whole system of moving people and goods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「运输」，指整套运送系统。

entries.definition: A channel for ideas or messages, the abstract sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「媒介」，即抽象的含义。

entries.definition: One that carries, used of people, bags or germs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「携带者」，用于人、袋子或病菌。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the carrying root and the double life of the word as transport and as medium.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「运载」词根，以及这个词作为交通工具与媒介的双重身份。

normal.en: Vehicle comes from a Latin verb meaning to carry.
normal.cn: vehicle 出自一个意为「运载」的拉丁动词。

normal.en: Motor vehicle is the formal term in law and insurance.
normal.cn: motor vehicle 是法律与保险里的正式说法。

normal.en: A vehicle for change is a means, not a machine.
normal.cn: a vehicle for change 指手段，不是机器。

normal.en: Convey and voyage share the same root as vehicle.
normal.cn: convey 与 voyage 和 vehicle 同根。

normal.en: The plural is vehicles, with the k sound kept before the s.
normal.cn: 复数是 vehicles，k 音在 s 前仍然保留。

abstract.en: Everything in the word is about being carried: a body, an idea, a germ, a colour.
abstract.cn: 这个词说的全是「被载着」：身体、想法、病菌、颜色。

abstract.en: A vehicle changes the reach of what it carries; the idea is the same size, the audience is not.
abstract.cn: 交通工具改变的是所载之物的抵达范围；想法没变大，听众变大了。

abstract.en: The oldest sense was any means; modern life narrowed it to wheels and then quietly reopened it.
abstract.cn: 最古老的含义是任何手段；现代生活把它收窄到车轮，又悄悄打开。

examples.en: All vehicles must stop at the red light.
examples.cn: 所有车辆必须在红灯前停下。

examples.en: The film became a vehicle for young actors.
examples.cn: 这部电影成了年轻演员展示自己的载体。

examples.en: Mosquitoes are a vehicle for several diseases.
examples.cn: 蚊子是几种疾病的传播媒介。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为爱扣」——为爱扣上车门，一路载着走：车辆

root: 源自拉丁语名词 vehiculum「运输手段」（动词 vehere「运载」），经法语 véhicule 进入英语；同族词有 convey、voyage、vehicular。

sensesIntro.en: Vehicle begins as anything that carries, narrows to cars, then widens back to ideas, germs and paint.
sensesIntro.cn: vehicle 起初指一切运载之物，收窄为车辆，又扩回思想、病菌与颜料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cart at the platform, doors open, passengers and their plans getting off together.
core.cn: 核心意象：站台边的一辆车，门一开，乘客和他们的计划一起下来。

branches.en: ROAD LINE: machines with wheels or engines.
branches.cn: 道路线：有轮或发动机的机器。

branches.en: ART LINE: a story that carries a point of view.
branches.cn: 艺术线：承载观点的小说或影片。

branches.en: CHANNEL LINE: water or insects carrying disease.
branches.cn: 渠道线：带病的水或昆虫。

branches.en: PAINT LINE: the liquid that holds pigment.
branches.cn: 颜料线：承载颜料的媒介。

branches.en: CONTRAST: transport is the system, a vehicle is one machine in it.
branches.cn: 对照线：transport 是系统，vehicle 是其中一台机器。

intro.en: Vehicle is a Latin noun; its relatives mostly come from the same carrying verb with other prefixes.
intro.cn: vehicle 是拉丁名词，亲属词多由同一运载动词加不同前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is vehere, to carry, giving vehiculum and also vector and convehere.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 vehere「运载」，派生出 vehiculum，也派生出 vector 与 convehere。

items.example: It is the core of vehicle.
It names the thing that carries.
It is the same journey idea.
items.exampleCN: 它带有同样的旅程观念。

items.structure: French noun from the same verb

definition_zh: 版本；说法、描述；（软件、文件的）修订本；改编本
definition_en: a particular form of something that differs from other forms of it, such as a copy, an account, or an edition
core_image: 同一份稿子被改了又改，桌上摊着好几份，每一份都略有不同
scene: 编辑把同一篇文章的三个版本并排打开，逐段比较。The final version was shorter than the first one by two pages.
sceneCN: 这里 version 是「版本」（第 1 个义项：与同一事物的其他形式不同的某个形态）；句意为最终版本比第一版短了两页。几份稿子并排放在桌上，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：版本；说法；改编本；译文

collocations.phrase: a film version of the novel

derivatives.zh: 加形容词后缀构成，义为「与版本有关的」
加 -ing 构成，义为「版本管理、版本化」
同一拉丁词根 vert-「转」构成，义为「多才多艺的；多用途的」
同一词根构成，义为「转换；改变信仰」

senses.title: One form among many
senses.titleCN: 版本：众多形态中的一种
senses.definition: a particular form of something, in which it differs from other forms of the same thing
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的一种特定形态，与其他形态有所差别
senses.example: The paper published a longer version of the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 报纸刊登了那次访谈的较长版本。
senses.why: Latin vertere means to turn; a version is the same matter turned a little differently.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vertere 意为「转」；version 就是同一件事被稍稍转了个角度。

senses.title: One person's account
senses.titleCN: 说法：某人对事情的一种讲法
senses.definition: one person's account of an event, especially when others may tell it differently
senses.definitionCN: 某人对一件事的讲述，尤指他人可能有不同讲法时
senses.example: The two witnesses gave very different versions of the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 两名证人对事故的说法大相径庭。
senses.why: An account is also a turning: the same event passes through one perspective and comes out shaped by it.
senses.whyCN: 讲述同样是一种转动：同一件事经过一个人的视角，出来时已被这个视角塑形。

senses.title: An edition or revision
senses.titleCN: 修订本：经过修改的一版
senses.definition: a revised or updated edition of a text, file or product
senses.definitionCN: 文本、文件或产品经过修改更新的一个版本
senses.example: This is the third version of the manual, and it is much clearer.
senses.exampleCN: 这是手册的第三版，清楚多了。
senses.why: Each revision turns the draft once more, and the newest turn is what users install.
senses.whyCN: 每一次修订都把稿子再转一次，最新的那一转就是用户安装的那个。

senses.title: An adaptation
senses.titleCN: 改编本：由原作改成的形式
senses.definition: a form of a work that has been adapted for another medium or audience
senses.definitionCN: 为另一种媒介或受众改编而成的作品形式
senses.example: The film version leaves out the youngest brother entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 电影改编版把最小的弟弟整个删掉了。
senses.why: Moving a story to the screen is a literal turning: the same characters now seen from a new side.
senses.whyCN: 把故事搬上银幕是一种字面意义上的转动：同一些人物从新的方向被看见。

senses.title: A specific release of software
senses.titleCN: 软件的一个具体发行版
senses.definition: a numbered release of a program or document, used to track changes over time
senses.definitionCN: 带编号的程序或文档发行版本，用于追踪变化
senses.example: Please update to version 4.2 before sending the file.
senses.exampleCN: 发送文件之前请更新到 4.2 版。
senses.why: In modern use the turning is numbered: each fix produces one more version on the record.
senses.whyCN: 在现代用法里，这种转动被编了号：每修一处，记录上就多一个版本。

intro.en: Version comes from the Latin verb 'to turn', and the whole family follows that image of turning.
intro.cn: version 源自拉丁语表示「转」的动词，整个词族都沿着这一转动的意象展开。

items.en: The verb vertere meant 'to turn, turn around, change'; it lies behind convert, revert and reverse.
items.cn: 动词 vertere 意为「转、回转、改变」，它是 convert、revert、reverse 背后的词。

items.en: Versio meant 'a turning, a change, a translation'; the noun names the act of turning something.
items.cn: versio 意为「转动、改变、翻译」，这一名词指把某物转一次这件事。

items.en: Old French borrowed the word for a translation or rendering of a text.
items.cn: 古法语借入这个词，指文本的翻译或转写。

items.en: English adopted version first for translations, then for any form differing from another.
items.cn: 英语最初用 version 指译本，后来泛指与其他形式有别的任一形态。

items.en: Publishing, then computing, turned it into a counting word: first version, final version, version number.
items.cn: 出版业再到计算机业把它变成计数词：第一版、最终版、版本号。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin turn-root; the near-meaning group gathers words for forms and accounts.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「转」词根构成的词；近义组收表示形态与说法的词。

entries.definition: The act of turning something into another form or use.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「转换、转变」，指把某物变成另一形态或用途。

entries.definition: To turn the other way round; the opposite direction of the same turn.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「颠倒、反转」，是同一转动的相反方向。

entries.definition: Turned apart, hence different; a family voice of the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多样的」，本义为「转向不同方向」。

entries.definition: Able to turn to many uses or skills.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「多才多艺的、多用途的」，即能转向许多用途。

entries.definition: One printing or published form of a text, usually revised.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「版次」，指文本的一次印行，通常经过修订。

entries.definition: A report or description of what happened; the everyday word for sense 02.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「叙述、说法」，是义项 02 的日常词。

entries.definition: A form that differs slightly, often in spelling or wording.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「变体」，指略有差别的形式，多指拼写或措辞。

entries.definition: A performance or translation of a work, stressing the performer's version.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「演绎、译文」，强调表演者或译者的处理。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb vertere and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语动词 vertere，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: version shares its root with turn: each version is the same thing turned again.
normal.cn: version 与 turn 同根：每个版本都是同一件东西又转过一次。

normal.en: Different witnesses, different versions: the same event turned through different eyes.
normal.cn: 不同的证人给出不同的说法：同一件事经过不同的眼睛转动一次。

normal.en: Software asks for a version number; a novel asks for a film version.
normal.cn: 软件要的是版本号；小说要的是电影改编版。

normal.en: The original version stays the reference while later versions move away from it.
normal.cn: 原版始终是参照，后来的版本则离它越来越远。

normal.en: Ver- inside version echoes vertere, the turning verb of Latin.
normal.cn: version 里的 ver- 呼应 vertere，即拉丁语那个「转」的动词。

abstract.en: Picture one sheet of paper on a turntable: each small rotation shows a slightly different face, and each face is a version.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸放在转盘上：每一次微转都露出略不同的正面，每一面都是一个版本。

abstract.en: A version is never the thing itself, only a way of seeing it, which is why accounts can disagree.
abstract.cn: 版本从来不是事物本身，只是一种看它的方式，所以各种说法可以彼此矛盾。

abstract.en: The word travels from clay tablets to code without changing its logic: turn, compare, number.
abstract.cn: 这个词从泥板一路走到代码，逻辑却没变：转动、比较、编号。

examples.en: This is an older version of the map, without the new road.
examples.cn: 这是这幅地图的旧版本，上面还没有那条新路。

examples.en: Each witness told a slightly different version of the night.
examples.cn: 每个证人对那一夜的讲述都略有不同。

examples.en: The app will not open until you install the latest version.
examples.cn: 不安装最新版本，这个应用就打不开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我（ver）想（sion）」——同一个故事，我想的说法和别人不一样：版本

root: 源自拉丁语 versio「转动、翻译」，来自动词 vertere「转」；经古法语进入英语；同族词有 convert、reverse、diverse、versatile。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of version all rest on one turning: the same matter presented in another form, as an account, an edition, an adaptation, or a numbered release.
sensesIntro.cn: version 的五个义项都建立在一次转之上：同一件事以另一种形态出现，或是说法、或是修订本、或是改编、或是编号发行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sheets of one article side by side on a desk, each slightly changed.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一篇文章的几份稿子并排在桌上，每份都略有变化。

branches.en: FORM LINE: the noun names any one form of many.
branches.cn: 形态线：名词指众多形态中的任意一种。

branches.en: VOICE LINE: an account is the event turned through one person.
branches.cn: 说法线：说法就是事件经过某个人转动后的样子。

branches.en: COUNT LINE: editions and software releases are numbered turns.
branches.cn: 计数线：版本与软件发行都是被编号的一次转动。

branches.en: MEDIUM LINE: the story turns from page to screen.
branches.cn: 媒介线：故事从纸面转到银幕。

branches.en: CONTRAST: the original is the point from which every version departs.
branches.cn: 对照线：原版是所有版本由之离开的那个点。

intro.en: Version is a Latin noun stem with an English noun ending; the turning root stays visible inside it.
intro.cn: version 是拉丁语名词词干加英语名词词尾，其中的「转」词根仍清晰可见。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is documented: vertere, with the noun versio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础有据可查：动词 vertere 及其名词 versio。

items.example: It forms version from the stem.

definition_zh: 非常；很；（限定用法）正是那个；极端的
definition_en: to a high degree, and, before a noun, the actual or exact one
core_image: 温度计的红柱一路顶到最上面那格
scene: 面试官看完简历，抬头说了一句：这份作品集非常出色。The interviewer said that the portfolio was very impressive.
sceneCN: 这里 very 是「非常」（第 1 个义项：表示程度很高）；句意为面试官说这份作品集非常出色。温度计顶格的那个画面就是这个副词给人的感觉。

derivatives.zh: 短语，义为「非常；十分」
古旧副词，义为「确实地；真正地」

senses.title: To a high degree
senses.definition: used to strengthen an adjective or another adverb
senses.definitionCN: 用来加强形容词或副词的程度
senses.example: The interviewer said the portfolio was very impressive.
senses.exampleCN: 面试官说这份作品集非常出色。
senses.why: The oldest job of the word is simply to push a quality higher.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的作用，就是把某种性质往上推高。

senses.title: In a high degree with verbs
senses.definition: used with some verbs and participles to mean greatly
senses.definitionCN: 与某些动词或分词连用，表示程度很高
senses.example: She was very pleased with the result.
senses.exampleCN: 她对结果非常满意。
senses.why: With a participle the same word shifts from modifying a quality to modifying an action.
senses.whyCN: 与分词连用时，同一个词从修饰性质转为修饰动作。

senses.title: The actual or exact one
senses.definition: used before a noun to single out the exact person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，指出正是某个人或某个事物
senses.example: That is the very book I was looking for.
senses.exampleCN: 那正是我在找的那本书。
senses.why: Pointing at one exact item is a short step from pushing a quality to its limit.
senses.whyCN: 从把性质推向极限，到指出唯一确切的那一个，只是一小步。

senses.title: The extreme end of something
senses.definition: used with a noun to mean the extreme or utmost
senses.definitionCN: 与名词连用，表示极端或极致
senses.example: They searched to the very end of the cave.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一直搜到洞穴的最深处。
senses.why: If a quality is pushed to the top, the noun that carries it is at its extreme.
senses.whyCN: 性质既被推到顶端，承载它的名词也就处在极端处。

senses.title: Used to add force in speech
senses.definition: used in speech for emphasis, as in the very idea
senses.definitionCN: 用于口语中加强语气，如 the very idea
senses.example: The very idea of moving abroad frightened him.
senses.exampleCN: 一想到要搬到国外，他就害怕。
senses.why: Emphasis in speech takes the same intensifying force and turns it on an idea.
senses.whyCN: 口语里的强调，把这股加强的力量转而用在某个念头上。

intro.en: Very began as a French adjective meaning true, and turned into the intensifier we use today.
intro.cn: very 最初是法语中意为「真实的」的形容词，后来变成今天的程度副词。

items.en: Verus meant true, and verax named the one who tells the truth.
items.cn: verus 意为真实的，verax 指说真话的人。

items.en: French verai carried the sense of genuine into everyday speech.
items.cn: 法语 verai 把「真正的」这一含义带入日常口语。

items.en: English verray first meant true or real, as in a verray friend.
items.cn: 中世纪英语 verray 最初意为真实的，如 a verray friend（真正的朋友）。

items.en: Placed before an adjective, it began to mean in a true degree, hence greatly.
items.cn: 放在形容词前时，它开始表示「真正地…」，进而表示「非常」。

items.en: The old sense survives only in fixed phrases such as the very same.
items.cn: 旧义如今只保留在 the very same 这类固定短语中。

note.en: The first group holds the small family of forms, the second the intensifiers and their opposites.
note.cn: 第一组是同族的小词群，第二组是程度副词及其反义说法。

entries.definition: truly, in old use
to a great degree
to check that something is true
to change or differ
to the highest degree
fairly, to a moderate degree
precise, with nothing added
to a small degree

normalIntro.en: From a Latin word for true to a word that simply turns the volume up: very has kept only its force.
normalIntro.cn: 从拉丁语中表示「真实」的词，到只负责把音量调大的词：very 只留下了那股加强的力量。

normal.en: Very and verify share the Latin root verus, true.
normal.cn: very 与 verify 同出拉丁语 verus（真实的）。

normal.en: Before a noun it means exact: the very man.
normal.cn: 放在名词前表示确切：the very man（正是那个人）。

normal.en: Before an adjective it means greatly: very cold.
normal.cn: 放在形容词前表示程度高：very cold（很冷）。

normal.en: It does not modify verbs directly; say very much like, not very like.
normal.cn: 它不直接修饰动词；要说 very much like，而非 very like。

normal.en: Comparative forms verier and veriest survive only in old books.
normal.cn: 比较级 verier、最高级 veriest 只存在于旧书中。

abstract.en: Picture a thermometer whose red line goes to the top mark.
abstract.cn: 想一支温度计的红线顶到最上面一格。

abstract.en: Feel a speaker leaning forward to press one word harder.
abstract.cn: 感受说话人身子前倾，把某一个词压得更重。

abstract.en: See a spotlight picking out one single chair on a stage.
abstract.cn: 想聚光灯在舞台上圈出唯一一把椅子。

examples.en: The soup is very hot, so let it cool for a minute.
examples.cn: 汤很烫，让它凉一分钟。

examples.en: This is the very place where the two roads meet.
examples.cn: 这里正是两条路交汇的地方。

examples.en: He was not very happy about the change of plan.
examples.cn: 他对计划的变更不太满意。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外瑞」——外边那位瑞哥嗓门特别大，一说就是「非常」响。

root: 拉丁语 verus（真实的）→ 古法语 verai → 中世纪英语 verray（真正的）→ 现代英语 very（非常）

sensesIntro.en: One little word grows from true, through truly to a plain intensifier, and keeps a second life as exactly that one.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个小词从「真实」出发，经「真正地」变成纯粹的程度副词，又保留了「正是那一个」的第二重身份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thermometer pushed to its top mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：温度计被推到最高那一格。

branches.en: The degree branch: a portfolio called impressive.
branches.cn: 程度分支：被称作出色的作品集。

branches.en: The verb branch: very pleased with the result.
branches.cn: 动词分支：对结果非常满意。

branches.en: The pointing branch: the very book on the shelf.
branches.cn: 指认分支：架上正是那本书。

branches.en: The extreme branch: the very end of the cave.
branches.cn: 极端分支：洞穴的最深处。

branches.en: The emphasis branch: the very idea frightens him.
branches.cn: 强调分支：光是这个念头就让他害怕。

intro.en: There is no living prefix here; the old root ver- (true) survives mainly inside longer words.
intro.cn: 这个词没有可拆的活前缀，古词根 ver-（真实）主要存活在更长的词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin verus gave French verai and English very; the same root also built verify, verity, and verdict.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 verus 派生法语 verai 与英语 very，同一词根还构成 verify、verity、verdict。

items.example: Ver- hides inside very as the sense of the genuine.
items.exampleCN: ver- 藏在 very 里，是「真正」的含义。

items.example: Very first meant in a true way.
items.exampleCN: very 最初表示「以真实的方式」。

items.example: We verify the figures before printing.
items.exampleCN: 付印前我们会核实这些数字。

items.meaning: a true saying by a jury
items.example: The jury returned a verdict of not guilty.
The verity of the claim was never in doubt.
items.exampleCN: 这一说法的真实性从未被怀疑。

items.example: She enjoyed the trip very much.
They wore the very same coat.
items.exampleCN: 他们穿的是完全相同的外套。

items.example: The film was not very long.

definition_zh: 兽医；老兵；审查；检查
definition_en: an animal doctor, or a person who has served in the armed forces; as a verb, to check someone or something carefully before acceptance
core_image: 给动物看病的人：一件白大褂，面前站着一只不安的小狗
scene: 宠物诊所里，主人轻轻按住小猫的爪子。The vet examined the injured paw carefully before giving the vaccine.
sceneCN: 这里 vet 是「兽医」（第 1 个义项：给动物治病的医生）；句意是兽医在打疫苗前仔细检查受伤的爪子。

pos.zh: 审查；检查（人或物）是否合格

collocations.phrase: take the dog to the vet

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语 veteranus（老兵）演变而来，本词 vet 是其口语缩略；义为「老兵；经验丰富的人」
veteran 同族形容词，义为「兽医的；动物医疗的」

senses.title: An animal doctor
senses.definition: a person trained to give medical care to sick or injured animals
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、给生病或受伤动物提供医疗照护的人
senses.example: The vet gave the puppy a check-up.
senses.exampleCN: 兽医给小狗做了一次体检。
senses.why: The word is short for veterinary surgeon, the professional who treats animals instead of people.
senses.whyCN: 本词是 veterinary surgeon（兽医外科医生）的口语缩略，指给动物而非人类治病的职业者，核心画面就是白大褂加小动物。

senses.title: A former soldier
senses.definition: a person who has served for a long time or in a war, especially in the armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 长期服役或经历过战争的人，尤指退伍军人
senses.example: The old vet marched at the head of the parade.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老兵走在游行队伍的最前面。
senses.why: It is the colloquial shortening of veteran, from Latin veteranus meaning one who has grown old in service.
senses.whyCN: 它是 veteran 的口语缩略；拉丁语 veteranus 指「在服役中变老的人」，所以引申为身经百战的老兵。

senses.title: An experienced person in a field
senses.definition: someone with long experience in a particular field or organization
senses.definitionCN: 在某一领域或组织中经验丰富的人
senses.example: She is a vet of the film industry, having produced movies for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 她是电影界的老手，制作电影已有三十年。
senses.why: Long service in the army extends metaphorically to long service anywhere, so the old hand and the old soldier share one word.
senses.whyCN: 军中的长期服役被隐喻推广到任何领域的长期资历，于是「老资格的人」与「老兵」共用同一个词。

senses.title: To check carefully before acceptance
senses.definition: to examine someone or something carefully to make sure they are suitable or safe
senses.definitionCN: 仔细审查某人或某物，确认其合适或安全
senses.example: Every employee is vetted before joining the team.
senses.exampleCN: 每位员工入职前都要经过审查。
senses.why: A doctor examines an animal thoroughly before treating it; that thorough inspection was extended to scrutinizing people and documents.
senses.whyCN: 兽医接诊前要先对动物做彻底检查，这种彻底查验被引申为对人员、文件的严格甄别审查。

senses.title: To treat an animal as a vet
senses.definition: to work as a vet, giving medical treatment to animals
senses.definitionCN: 以兽医身份工作，为动物进行治疗
senses.example: He has vetted farm animals in this village for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在这座村子给家畜看病已有二十年。
senses.why: The profession name naturally turns into a verb for doing the profession's work, just like nurse or coach.
senses.whyCN: 职业名词自然转为动词表示从事该职业的工作，正如 nurse（护理）、coach（执教）一样。

intro.en: Vet is a double shortening: veterinary surgeon for the animal doctor, and veteran for the old soldier.
intro.cn: vet 是双重缩略：作为「兽医」是 veterinary surgeon 的缩略；作为「老兵」是 veteran 的缩略。

items.en: veteranus meant 'aged, one who has served long', from vetus, 'old'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 veteranus 意为「年长的、长期服役的」，词根 vetus 意为「老」。

items.en: veterinarius described things relating to beasts of burden, the root of veterinary.
items.cn: 拉丁语 veterinarius 描述与驮兽相关的事物，是 veterinary 的来源。

items.en: Veteran entered English for old soldiers; veterinary surgeon named the animal doctor.
items.cn: veteran 于十七至十九世纪进入英语，指老兵；veterinary surgeon 指动物医生。

items.en: Both long titles were clipped to vet in everyday speech.
items.cn: 在日常口语中，两个冗长的头衔都被缩短成 vet。

items.en: The noun vet was turned into a verb meaning to scrutinize before acceptance.
items.cn: 名词 vet 又转为动词，表示「录用前的审查甄别」。

note.en: Watch the clipped forms: vet comes from two long words, and neighbors like veto only look alike.
note.cn: 注意缩略形式：vet 来自两个长词，而 veto（否决）等邻居只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: an official power to reject a decision or proposal
entries.definitionCN: 否决权；否决。只是拼写相近，词源不同（拉丁语 vetare，禁止）。

entries.definition: a person with long experience, especially a former soldier
entries.definitionCN: 老兵；经验丰富者。vet 作「老兵」解时正是它的口语缩略。

entries.definition: relating to the medical care of animals
entries.definitionCN: 兽医的；动物医疗的。vet 作「兽医」解时源自其首音节。

entries.definition: a doctor who treats human patients
entries.definitionCN: 医生；内科医生。对象是人类，与兽医保卫的对象相对。

entries.definition: a person who tests or inspects others formally
entries.definitionCN: 审查者；检查者。与 vet 动词义的「甄别审查」相近，但更正式。

entries.definition: to examine something very carefully
entries.definitionCN: 仔细审查。与 vet 的动词义几乎重合，但不含「录用前把关」的语感。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks built from the word's real history and uses.
normalIntro.cn: 基于词源与真实用法的五条联想。

normal.en: Vet clips veterinary surgeon: the vet vets your pet.
normal.cn: vet 是 veterinary surgeon 的缩略：兽医给宠物看病（vet your pet）。

normal.en: Vet also clips veteran: the war vet sits beside the dog vet.
normal.cn: vet 也是 veteran 的缩略：老兵与兽医共用一个短词。

normal.en: To vet a candidate is to give him a full check-up, like an animal at the clinic.
normal.cn: 审查候选人类似兽医接诊：先做全面「体检」再放行。

normal.en: Latin vetus means old; veterans are those grown old in service.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根 vetus 意为「老」，老兵就是服役到老的人。

normal.en: Verb forms double the T: vet, vetted, vetting.
normal.cn: 动词变化双写 T：vet, vetted, vetting。

abstract.en: Picture a white coat with one pocket for pills and another for medals.
abstract.cn: 想象一件白大褂，一个口袋装药片，另一个装勋章。

abstract.en: Imagine a small dog waiting quietly under the clinic lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象诊灯下安静等待的小狗。

abstract.en: Feel a gatekeeper's stamp: checked, approved, allowed through.
abstract.cn: 感受把关者的印章：查毕、合格、放行。

examples.en: We took the sick cat to the vet this morning.
examples.cn: 今天早上我们带生病的猫去看兽医。

examples.en: His grandfather was a navy vet who loved telling stories.
examples.cn: 他的祖父是位海军老兵，爱讲故事。

examples.en: All news reports are vetted before publication.
examples.cn: 所有新闻报道发表前都要经过审查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂它」——兽医的工作就是喂它、护理它；老兵回营也是为了有口饭「喂它」。

root: vet 作名词有两条来源：一是 veterinary（拉丁语 veterinarius「与驮兽有关的」）的缩略，指兽医；二是 veteran（拉丁语 veteranus，词根 vetus「老」）的缩略，指老兵。动词义由「彻底检查」引申而来。

sensesIntro.en: From the animal doctor and the old soldier, the word stretches to experienced hands and then to the act of scrutiny.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「兽医」「老兵」两个名词核心，延伸出「老手」的比喻义，再引申出动词「审查」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a short white coat that serves animals, soldiers, and the checkpoint
core.cn: 核心意象：一件服务动物、军人，并守在检查关卡前的白大褂

branches.en: The clinic work
branches.cn: 诊所里的诊疗工作，从名词职业到动词行医。

branches.en: The battle-tested soldier
branches.cn: 身经百战的退伍军人。

branches.en: The veteran of any trade
branches.cn: 任何行业的资深老手。

branches.en: The thorough check before trust
branches.cn: 信任之前的彻底核查。

branches.en: From inspection to clearance
branches.cn: 从检查到放行，把关的完整闭环。

intro.en: The family of vet- rests on Latin vetus, old, and branches into medicine, war, and checking.
intro.cn: vet- 词族建立在拉丁语 vetus（老）之上，分支延伸到医疗、战争与审查领域。

latinIntro.en: Latin relatives that share the root of growing old in service.
latinIntro.cn: 共享「服役至老」这一词根的拉丁同源词。

items.example: veterani were settled on farmland after service
items.exampleCN: 退伍老兵战后被安置到农田。

derivatives.zh: vet 的全形来源之一，义为「老兵；老手」
vet 的全形来源之一，义为「兽医的」

definition_zh: 经由；经过（某地）；通过、借助（某人或某手段）
definition_en: by way of a place, or by means of a person or method
core_image: 一条路线在纸上转弯，绕过一座山，最后才到达目的地
scene: 邮件在三个城市之间转了一圈，最后才落到桌上。We flew to Rome via Zurich.
sceneCN: 这里 via 是「经由某地」（第 1 个义项：路线经过某地）；句意为我们先飞到苏黎世，再转去罗马。那条绕过山再到的路线，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 介词：经由、经过；通过、借助

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「高架桥」，与 via 同源于拉丁语 via「道路」
动词，义为「偏离」，同源于拉丁语 via
形容词，义为「明显的」，字面义为「在路上迎面遇上」，同根
形容词，义为「琐碎的」，字面义为「三岔路口的」，同根

senses.title: By way of a place
senses.titleCN: 经由某地：路线经过而不停留
senses.definition: travelling through a place on the way to another
senses.definitionCN: 在前往另一地途中经过某地
senses.example: We flew to Rome via Zurich.
senses.exampleCN: 我们先飞到苏黎世，再转去罗马。
senses.why: Latin via is a road; the preposition simply names the road taken without claiming a stop.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 via 就是道路；这个介词只说走的是哪条路，并不表示停下来。

senses.title: By means of
senses.titleCN: 通过、借助：靠某种手段完成
senses.definition: by means of a particular method, person or service
senses.definitionCN: 通过某种方法、人或服务实现
senses.example: We sent the documents via email to save time.
senses.exampleCN: 为了省时间，我们通过电子邮件发了文件。
senses.why: The road becomes a figure of speech: the channel that carries the action.
senses.whyCN: 道路变成了比喻：承载这个动作的通道。

senses.title: Through an intermediary
senses.titleCN: 经某人转手：不直接对接
senses.definition: through a person or office acting in between
senses.definitionCN: 通过居间的人或机构
senses.example: The message reached him via his assistant.
senses.exampleCN: 消息通过他的助理传到了他那里。
senses.why: The route now runs through a person rather than through a town.
senses.whyCN: 路线这次穿过的是一个人，而不是一座城镇。

senses.title: Through a route or medium
senses.titleCN: 通过某一路径或媒介：抽象通道
senses.definition: through a particular route, path or medium
senses.definitionCN: 通过特定路径或媒介
senses.example: Data travels via underground cables to the other building.
senses.exampleCN: 数据经地下电缆传到另一栋楼。
senses.why: A cable is a road for electricity, and the word applies without any change of form.
senses.whyCN: 电缆是电的道路，这个词不再变形就直接用上了。

intro.en: Via is the Latin noun for road, taken whole into English and pressed into service as a preposition.
intro.cn: via 是拉丁语里表示「道路」的名词，整块进入英语后被用作介词。

items.en: The noun via meant a road, way or street, and also a method.
items.cn: 名词 via 意为道路、路径，也可指方法。

items.en: In phrases such as via Appia the ablative already worked as by way of, a road name in use.
items.cn: 在 via Appia 这类短语里，这个夺格形式已经带有「经……路」的意味。

items.en: English borrowed via in the eighteenth century as a preposition of route.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入 via，用作表路线的介词。

items.en: Rail, aviation and postal writing spread it through travel timetables.
items.cn: 铁路、航空与邮政文书把它普及到旅行时刻表里。

items.en: Modern usage adds the abstract sense, so documents now travel via email.
items.cn: 现代用法增添了抽象含义，于是文件可以通过邮件旅行。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin road root; the near-meaning group holds prepositions of route and means.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁「道路」词根；近义组收表示路线与手段的介词。

entries.definition: A road carried over a valley; literally a road leader.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「高架桥」，字面即「引路之桥」。

entries.definition: To leave the road; hence to stray.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「偏离」，字面即离开道路。

entries.definition: Literally lying in the road, hence plain to see.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明显的」，字面即「在路中遇到」。

entries.definition: Of a crossroads, hence common and slight.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「琐碎的」，由「三岔路口」引申为常见而轻微。

entries.definition: By way of, inside and out the other side.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「穿过」，从一头进、另一头出。

entries.definition: By means of, or past a point on a route.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「靠、经」，也可指路过某点。

entries.definition: In every part, stronger than via.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「遍及」，比 via 更强。

entries.definition: Following the length of a road or river.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「沿着」，顺着路或河的长度走。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the literal road and the modern habits of travel and mail.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用字面上的「道路」，以及现代出行与邮件的习惯。

normal.en: Via is Latin for road, and roads explain the word.
normal.cn: via 是拉丁语的「道路」，道路解释了它。

normal.en: Fly via Paris means Paris is on the way, not the destination.
normal.cn: fly via Paris 指巴黎在途中，不是目的地。

normal.en: Send it via email means the message takes a digital road.
normal.cn: send it via email 指消息走了一条数字的路。

normal.en: Obvious, deviate and trivial all come from the same road word.
normal.cn: obvious、deviate、trivial 都出自同一个「道路」词。

normal.en: Via does not mean in: you do not stop there for long.
normal.cn: via 不等于 in：你不在那里久留。

abstract.en: Via names the path rather than the place: it tells you how the thing got here.
abstract.cn: via 命名的是路径而非地点：它告诉你东西是怎么过来的。

abstract.en: Anything that moves needs a road, so the word stretches to cables, satellites and people.
abstract.cn: 凡会动的东西都需要一条路，于是这个词扩展到电缆、卫星和人。

abstract.en: To name the route is already to hint at the motive, which is why the same word covers means.
abstract.cn: 说出路线已经在暗示成因，所以同一个词也能表示手段。

examples.en: We returned home via the coast road.
examples.cn: 我们沿着海边公路回家。

examples.en: Please send your application via the website.
examples.cn: 请通过网站提交申请。

examples.en: He learned the news via a friend in the office.
examples.cn: 他从办公室的一位朋友那里得到这个消息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外啊」——外啊，外面这条路经过咱们这儿：经由

root: 直接来自拉丁语名词 via「道路、方法」，十八世纪起在英语中作介词使用；同根词有 viaduct、deviate、obvious、trivial。

sensesIntro.en: Via travels from a real road, to a method, to a person in between, to an abstract channel.
sensesIntro.cn: via 从真实的道路出发，走到方法、居间的人，再到抽象的通道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line on a map that bends around a hill before reaching the mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上一条线绕过小山，才到目的地。

branches.en: ROUTE LINE: a place passed on the way.
branches.cn: 路线线：途中经过的地点。

branches.en: METHOD LINE: the means by which it is done.
branches.cn: 方法线：办成事所借助的手段。

branches.en: PEOPLE LINE: a message relayed by someone else.
branches.cn: 人际线：由别人转达的消息。

branches.en: CABLE LINE: an abstract path or medium.
branches.cn: 线路线：抽象的路径或媒介。

branches.en: CONTRAST: via names the way, in names the place.
branches.cn: 对照线：via 说路，in 说地。

intro.en: Via has no affixes, but the Latin noun it comes from hides inside several English words.
intro.cn: via 没有词缀，但构成它的拉丁名词藏在好几个英语词里。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun via, road, survives in viaduct, deviate, obvious and trivial.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 via「道路」残留在 viaduct、deviate、obvious、trivial 里。

items.example: It forms deviate, to leave the road.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 deviate，即离开道路。

items.example: It forms obvious, in the way.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 obvious，即在路中遇到。

items.example: It forms trivial, of three roads.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 trivial，即三岔路口的。

definition_zh: 受害者；牺牲品、殉难者；遇难者；（事故、疾病的）受害者
definition_en: a person harmed, injured or killed as the result of a crime, accident or other event
core_image: 一队被牵去献祭的牲畜，脖子上系着彩带，走在前头
scene: 火灾过后，邻居们围在被烧黑的门口，不知道该说什么。The victims of the flood are still waiting for help.
sceneCN: 这里 victim 是「受害者」（第 1 个义项：在灾难或罪案中受到伤害的人）；句意为洪水的受害者仍在等待救援。被牵去献祭的牲畜，就是这个词最早的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：受害者；牺牲品、殉难者；遇难者

collocations.zh: 装可怜、摆出受害者姿态

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「使受害、迫害」，由本词加 -ize 构成
名词，义为「受害、迫害」
形容词，义为「无受害者的」，如 victimless crime
名词，义为「受害者身份」

senses.title: One harmed by another
senses.titleCN: 受害者：被罪案或他人伤害的人
senses.definition: a person harmed by a crime or by someone else’s action
senses.definitionCN: 被犯罪或他人行为伤害的人
senses.example: The victims of the flood are still waiting for help.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水的受害者仍在等待救援。
senses.why: Latin victima was the animal led to sacrifice; the modern sense keeps the picture of someone taken and harmed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 victima 是被牵去献祭的牲畜；现代含义仍保留「被夺去并受伤害」的画面。

senses.title: One killed or injured
senses.titleCN: 遇难者：在事故或灾害中伤亡的人
senses.definition: a person killed or injured in an accident or disaster
senses.definitionCN: 在事故或灾害中死亡或受伤的人
senses.example: Road victims have fallen since the speed limit changed.
senses.exampleCN: 限速改变后，道路事故的死伤者减少了。
senses.why: No agent is needed here; the harm comes from events, not from a criminal.
senses.whyCN: 这里不需要施害者：伤害来自事件，而不是罪犯。

senses.title: One suffering from illness
senses.definition: a person suffering from a disease or condition
senses.definitionCN: 受某种疾病或状况折磨的人
senses.example: Many victims of the disease do not know they have it.
senses.exampleCN: 许多患这种病的人并不知道自己有。
senses.why: Illness is treated as an outer force that takes prisoners, much like an accident.
senses.whyCN: 疾病被当成一种抓走人的外部力量，与事故相似。

senses.title: A sacrifice
senses.titleCN: 牺牲品：为了别的目的而被舍弃的人或物
senses.definition: someone or something given up for another purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为别的目的被舍弃的人或物
senses.example: The old building became a victim of the redevelopment plan.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老建筑成了重建计划的牺牲品。
senses.why: Buildings cannot feel pain, yet the pattern holds: something old is given up for something new.
senses.whyCN: 建筑不会感到疼痛，但模式仍在：旧的东西为新的东西被舍弃了。

senses.title: A self-chosen role
senses.titleCN: 装出的受害者：把自己当成被亏待的人
senses.definition: a role taken on by someone who claims unfair treatment
senses.definitionCN: 某人自称受到不公而摆出的姿态
senses.example: He always plays the victim when the plan goes wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 计划一出错，他就摆出受害者的姿态。
senses.why: The word turns ironic here: the person chooses the role instead of receiving it.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词带了反讽：角色是自己选的，而不是被强加的。

intro.en: Victim comes from Latin victima, a beast offered in sacrifice, and has kept the sense of being taken and harmed.
intro.cn: victim 来自拉丁语 victima「祭献用的牲畜」，一直保留着「被夺去并受伤害」的意思。

items.en: Victima named the animal led to the altar, chosen and given up.
items.cn: victima 指被牵上祭坛的牲畜，被选中并被舍弃。

items.en: The word belonged to the language of sacrifice, with its sense of a life taken.
items.cn: 这个词属于献祭的语言，含「夺走一条生命」的意思。

items.en: French kept victime for a creature sacrificed or killed, sacred or not.
items.cn: 法语保留 victime，指被献祭或被杀的生命，不论是否神圣。

items.en: English took victim in the fifteenth century, widening it to anyone who suffers harm.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 victim，扩展到任何受到伤害的人。

items.en: Modern usage applies it to crime, disaster, disease and, ironically, to a chosen pose.
items.cn: 现代用法把它用于罪案、灾害、疾病，甚至反讽地指一种自愿摆出的姿态。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the victim- family; the near-meaning group holds words for those who suffer or are lost.
note.cn: 形近组沿 victim- 家族；近义组收表示受难者与损失的词。

entries.definition: To make someone a victim, often unfairly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使受害、迫害」，由本词构成。

entries.definition: The act of treating someone as a victim.
Having no harmed party, as in some crimes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无受害者的」。

entries.definition: The state of being a victim.
One who endures pain or illness, often long term.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「受苦者、患者」，多为长期。

entries.definition: One killed or wounded in fighting or an accident.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伤亡者」，多用于战争与事故。

entries.definition: One who lived through the same event, the other side.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「幸存者」，同一事件的另一面。

entries.definition: The one aimed at, before any harm is done.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「目标」，伤害尚未发生前的一方。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the sacrifice picture and the phrase fall victim to.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子使用「献祭」的画面与 fall victim to 这一搭配。

normal.en: Victim once meant the animal led to the altar.
normal.cn: victim 原本指被牵上祭坛的牲畜。

normal.en: Fall victim to a scam means the trick caught you.
normal.cn: fall victim to a scam 指你被这个骗局抓住了。

normal.en: Victims of a flood are harmed by weather, not by a criminal.
normal.cn: 洪水的受害者是被天气所害，而不是被罪犯。

normal.en: Victimize is the verb: to make someone a victim.
normal.cn: victimize 是动词：使某人成为受害者。

normal.en: Playing the victim is a choice of role, not a fact.
normal.cn: playing the victim 是一种角色选择，不是事实。

abstract.en: The word began in sacrifice, and every later use keeps the shape of a life given up for something else.
abstract.cn: 这个词始于献祭，此后每种用法都保留着「为别的东西交出生命」的形状。

abstract.en: A victim is defined by what happened to them, which is why the word is passive in grammar and in feeling.
abstract.cn: 受害者是由遭遇定义的，所以这个词在语法和情感上都是被动的。

abstract.en: Naming someone a victim gives them sympathy but takes away agency, a tension the word never resolves.
abstract.cn: 称某人为受害者，给了他同情却拿走了主动性，这个矛盾这个词从未解决。

examples.en: The charity helps victims of domestic violence.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构帮助家庭暴力的受害者。

examples.en: Many small shops fell victim to the rise in rents.
examples.cn: 许多小店成了租金上涨的牺牲品。

examples.en: She was the victim of a cruel joke.
examples.cn: 她是一个恶作剧的受害者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维克提姆」——维克（围）克（制）提（他）姆（母亲）受害了：受害者

root: 源自拉丁语名词 victima「祭献用的牲畜」，经法语 victime 于十五世纪进入英语；同族词有 victimize、victimization、victimhood。

sensesIntro.en: Victim stretches from the sacrificed animal to crime, accidents, illness, lost buildings and a chosen pose.
sensesIntro.cn: victim 从被献祭的牲畜，延伸到罪案、事故、疾病、被拆的建筑与自愿摆出的姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an animal led to the altar with ribbons on its neck.
core.cn: 核心意象：一头脖子系着彩带、被牵向祭坛的牲畜。

branches.en: CRIME LINE: harmed by another person.
branches.cn: 罪案线：被他人所害。

branches.en: DISASTER LINE: injured by events.
branches.cn: 灾害线：被事件所伤。

branches.en: ILLNESS LINE: struck by disease.
branches.cn: 疾病线：被病痛击中。

branches.en: FIGURE LINE: a building given up, a role worn on purpose.
branches.cn: 比喻线：被舍弃的建筑，故意披上的角色。

branches.en: CONTRAST: a victim receives harm, a target is only aimed at.
branches.cn: 对照线：受害者已受到伤害，目标只是被瞄准。

intro.en: Victim is a complete Latin noun; English relatives add -ize, -ization, -hood and -less.
intro.cn: victim 是完整的拉丁名词，英语亲属词加 -ize、-ization、-hood、-less。

latinIntro.en: The single Latin form is victima, a ritual word without a clear further root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形式只有一个 victima，是礼仪用语，更早的词根并不明确。

definition_zh: 胜利；获胜；成功
definition_en: success in a contest, battle, or struggle against an opponent or a difficulty
core_image: 终场哨响，全队抱在一起跳起来
scene: 决赛最后一分钟，主队攻入一球，看台上的人全都站了起来。The home side celebrated a narrow victory over the champions.
sceneCN: 这里 victory 是「胜利」（第 1 个义项：在比赛、战斗或与对手、困难的较量中取得胜利）；句意为主队在主场以微弱优势战胜了冠军队。终场哨响时抱在一起的人就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ious 构成，义为「胜利的；获胜的」
加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「胜利地」
同源名词，义为「胜利者」

senses.title: Success in a contest or battle
senses.definition: the act of defeating an opponent in a game, fight, or war
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、战斗或战争中击败对手
senses.example: The home side celebrated a narrow victory over the champions.
senses.exampleCN: 主队庆祝以微弱优势战胜了冠军队。
senses.why: Latin victoria came from victor, the winner, and a winner is what a contest produces.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 victoria 来自 victor（胜者），而胜者正是竞争产生的结果。

senses.title: Success in a struggle against difficulty
senses.definition: success in overcoming a problem, illness, or obstacle
senses.definitionCN: 克服问题、疾病或障碍而取得成功
senses.example: Her recovery was a quiet victory over fear.
senses.exampleCN: 她的康复是一场无声的、战胜恐惧的胜利。
senses.why: The opponent need not be a person: a disease or a fear can be beaten too.
senses.whyCN: 对手不必是人：疾病、恐惧同样可以被战胜。

senses.title: An advantage gained for a cause
senses.definition: a result that proves right or helps a principle or group
senses.definitionCN: 证明某一主张正确、或有利于某一原则与群体的结果
senses.example: The ruling is a victory for press freedom.
senses.exampleCN: 这一裁定是新闻自由的胜利。
senses.why: When a court or an election settles a principle, the side that principle favours has won.
senses.whyCN: 当法院或选举就某原则定论时，该原则所支持的一方就等于获胜。

senses.title: In ancient use, the goddess of success
senses.definition: the Roman goddess who personified success
senses.definitionCN: 古罗马象征成功的女神维多利亚
senses.example: A statue of Victory stood at the head of the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅一端立着一尊胜利女神像。
senses.why: Rome turned abstract success into a goddess, and her name is this noun.
senses.whyCN: 古罗马把抽象的成功人格化为女神，女神的名称正是这个词。

senses.title: The moment of triumph in speech or writing
senses.definition: a report or celebration of a win, as in headlines
senses.definitionCN: 对胜利的报道或庆祝，如新闻标题中的用法
senses.example: News of the victory reached the capital by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 胜利的消息中午就传到了首都。
senses.why: Once news travels, the abstract win becomes a piece of news people pass on.
senses.whyCN: 消息一旦传开，抽象的胜利就成了一条被人们转述的新闻。

intro.en: Victory goes back to Latin victoria, from victor, the one who wins.
intro.cn: victory 追溯至拉丁语 victoria，来自 victor（胜者）。

items.en: Vincere meant to conquer, and victor named the one who conquered.
items.cn: vincere 意为征服，victor 指征服者。

items.en: Victoria was the abstract noun for the win itself, and also a goddess.
items.cn: victoria 既是「胜利」这一抽象名词，也是一位女神。

items.en: French victoire carried the word toward English.
items.cn: 法语 victoire 把该词带向英语。

items.en: English took victory for a win in battle or in argument.
items.cn: 中世纪英语以 victory 指战斗或辩论中的胜利。

items.en: Sport and politics widened it to games, elections, and moral causes.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到比赛、选举与道义主张。

note.en: The first group holds the victor family, the second the close words for winning and losing.
note.cn: 第一组是 victor 词族，第二组是表示胜负的相近词。

entries.definition: the one who wins
having won
in a winning way
to make someone a victim
a great and public win
the reaching of a goal
the taking of land by force
a loss to an opponent

normalIntro.en: From the Latin goddess of success to the final score of a match: victory always ends a contest.
normalIntro.cn: 从拉丁语的成功女神到比赛的最终比分：victory 总在为一场较量收尾。

normal.en: Victory and victim look alike but have no common Latin root.
normal.cn: victory 与 victim 形似，却没有共同的拉丁词根。

normal.en: Drop the -y and add -or for victor, the winner.
normal.cn: 去掉 -y 加 -or 即 victor，获胜的人。

normal.en: Victorious adds -ious, like glorious.
normal.cn: victorious 加 -ious，如同 glorious。

normal.en: The plural changes y to ies: victories.
normal.cn: 复数 y 变 ies：victories。

normal.en: V is the sign of the Roman victory goddess on coins.
normal.cn: 古罗马钱币上的 V 就是胜利女神的标记。

abstract.en: See the scoreboard freeze at one goal ahead.
abstract.cn: 想记分牌定格在领先一球。

abstract.en: Hear a whole stand breathe out at the final whistle.
abstract.cn: 听终场哨响时整片看台一起呼气。

abstract.en: Picture a stone goddess with wings at the hall door.
abstract.cn: 想大厅门口一尊带翅膀的石女神。

examples.en: The team has now won three victories in a row.
examples.cn: 这支队伍如今已连赢三场。

examples.en: The law was seen as a victory for small farmers.
examples.cn: 这项法律被视为小农的胜利。

examples.en: They claimed victory before all the votes were counted.
examples.cn: 票还没数完他们就宣布获胜了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维克多利」——维克多力气最大，比赛拿了第一，胜利归他。

root: 拉丁语 vincere（征服）→ victor（胜者）→ victoria（胜利）→ 法语 victoire → 英语 victory

sensesIntro.en: One noun runs from a battle won, through a fear overcome and a principle upheld, to a goddess and a headline.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个名词从打赢一场仗，延伸到战胜恐惧、捍卫原则，再延伸到女神与新闻标题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a team leaping together as the whistle blows.
core.cn: 核心意象：终场哨响时全队一起跃起。

branches.en: The match branch: a narrow win at home.
branches.cn: 比赛分支：主场的险胜。

branches.en: The illness branch: a quiet win over fear.
branches.cn: 疾病分支：战胜恐惧的无声胜利。

branches.en: The cause branch: a ruling for press freedom.
branches.cn: 主张分支：有利于新闻自由的裁定。

branches.en: The altar branch: the winged goddess on her pedestal.
branches.cn: 神坛分支：柱座上的带翅膀女神。

branches.en: The news branch: word of the win reaching the capital.
branches.cn: 新闻分支：捷报传至首都。

intro.en: The root vinc-, vict- means to conquer; -or, -ory, and -ious build the family.
intro.cn: 词根 vinc-、vict- 意为征服，-or、-ory、-ious 构成这个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vincere gave victor and victoria; the stem vict- carries the sense of overcoming into every English form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vincere 派生 victor 与 victoria，词干 vict- 把「克服」之义带进每个英语形式。

items.example: Vict- carries the sense of winning.
A victor is the one who wins.
Victory names the state of having won.
items.exampleCN: victory 指已经获胜的状态。

items.example: Victorious means full of the win.
items.exampleCN: victorious 意为充满胜利感的。

items.example: They marched victoriously into the square.

items.exampleCN: 这个赛季带来六场胜利。

items.example: The triumph was marked by a parade.
items.exampleCN: 以游行的方式庆祝这次凯旋。

items.example: Defeat taught them more than victory.
items.exampleCN: 失败教会他们的比胜利更多。

definition_zh: 视频；录像；录制
definition_en: a recording of moving images, or the medium that carries them
core_image: 手机屏幕上，一段画面正在播放
scene: 面试前她对着手机录了一段自我介绍，反复看了三遍才发出去。She recorded a short video to introduce herself before the interview.
sceneCN: 这里 video 是「视频、录像」（第 1 个义项：由连续画面构成的影像作品）；句意为面试前她录了一小段视频介绍自己。手机屏幕上正在播放的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 合成词，义为「录像带」
合成词，义为「可视电话」
加后缀 -graphy 构成，义为「摄像；录像制作」

senses.title: A recording of moving pictures
senses.definition: a length of recorded moving images, with or without sound
senses.definitionCN: 一段录下的连续画面，可有声音也可无声
senses.example: She recorded a short video to introduce herself before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前她录了一小段视频介绍自己。
senses.why: Latin video means I see; a recording lets you see again what passed in front of a lens.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 video 意为「我看见」；录像让你再次看见曾经经过镜头的东西。

senses.title: The medium or signal that carries moving pictures
senses.definition: the system, signal, or equipment used to record and show moving images
senses.definitionCN: 用于录制和显示活动影像的系统、信号或设备
senses.example: The lecture was sent to remote students by video.
senses.exampleCN: 这堂课通过视频传给远端的学生。
senses.why: A recording is a thing; the channel that carries it is also called video, as in by video.
senses.whyCN: 录像是一个实物，而承载它的渠道也叫 video，如 by video。

senses.title: Short internet clips and their culture
senses.definition: a short clip made for online sharing, and the stream of such clips
senses.definitionCN: 为网络分享而制作的短片，以及这类内容的整体
senses.example: He spends an hour on short videos every night.
senses.exampleCN: 他每晚都刷一小时短视频。
senses.why: Once clips could be shared in seconds, the word grew into a genre of its own.
senses.whyCN: 短片可以秒速分享之后，这个词发展成了一个独立的内容类别。

senses.title: To record moving images
senses.definition: to make a recording of moving images with a camera or phone
senses.definitionCN: 用摄像机或手机录制活动影像
senses.example: They videoed the whole ceremony on a phone.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用手机把整个仪式都录了下来。
senses.why: Nouns turn into verbs easily in English, and video became one: to video an event.
senses.whyCN: 英语里名词容易转成动词，video 也是如此：把一场活动录下来。

senses.title: In teaching, visual material as a channel
senses.definition: recorded visual material used to teach or demonstrate
senses.definitionCN: 用于教学或示范的录制影像材料
senses.example: The course adds video to every unit.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课每个单元都加入影像材料。
senses.why: Classrooms borrow the word to name visual material that supports a lesson.
senses.whyCN: 课堂借用这个词来称呼辅助教学的影像材料。

intro.en: Video is a modern word taken straight from the Latin verb video, I see.
intro.cn: video 是近代直接取自拉丁动词 video（我看见）的词。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and video is its first person, I see.
items.cn: videre 意为看见，video 是它的第一人称形式「我看见」。

items.en: The Latin phrase video et taceo, I see and keep silent, shows the verb in use.
items.cn: 拉丁语短语 video et taceo（我看见而不语）正是该动词的用例。

items.en: Technical writers of the twentieth century used Latin stems for new media.
items.cn: 二十世纪的技术作者用拉丁词干给新媒介命名。

items.en: Video, from Latin through the sense of seeing, was coined against audio, I hear.
items.cn: video 与表示听见的 audio 相对，借「看见」之义造出。

items.en: It moved from equipment to recording to clips, and then to a verb.
items.cn: 它从设备转到录像，又转到短片，最后成为动词。

note.en: The first group holds compounds built on video, the second the media that compete with it.
note.cn: 第一组是由 video 构成的合成词，第二组是与视频并列的媒介。

entries.definition: magnetic tape for recording pictures
a phone that shows the caller
the making of video recordings
more than one recording
recorded sound
a short piece of a recording
recorded film or video material
a long recorded story on screen

normalIntro.en: Latin video, I see, is the whole story: whatever lets you see again is called video.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语 video（我看见）就是全部由来：凡是让你再看一遍的东西，都叫 video。

normal.en: Video and audio are a pair: I see against I hear.
normal.cn: video 与 audio 是一对：我看见对我听见。

normal.en: The plural is videos, plainly adding s.
normal.cn: 复数 videos，直接加 s。

normal.en: As a verb it takes -ed: they videoed the event.
normal.cn: 作动词时加 -ed：they videoed the event。

normal.en: Video calling keeps the noun before another noun.
normal.cn: video calling 是名词作定语。

normal.en: The Latin verb videre also gives visible and vision.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 videre 还派生 visible 与 vision。

abstract.en: See a small screen in a hand, a face speaking.
abstract.cn: 想手心里的小屏幕里有一张脸在说话。

abstract.en: Hear the click of a record button.
abstract.cn: 听录制键按下的一声轻响。

abstract.en: Picture a lens and an eye drawn side by side.
abstract.cn: 想一枚镜头和一只眼睛并排放着。

examples.en: The school posted a video of the concert online.
examples.cn: 学校把音乐会的视频发到了网上。

examples.en: Please video the meeting so absent staff can watch.
examples.cn: 请把会议录下来，好让缺席的同事观看。

examples.en: Video has largely replaced tape in newsrooms.
examples.cn: 在新闻编辑室里，视频已基本取代了磁带。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂迪欧」——喂，迪欧，快把刚才那一段录像发给我。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看见）的第一人称 video（我看见）→ 英语 video

sensesIntro.en: From a single Latin sentence, I see, the word grew into recordings, signals, online clips, a verb, and classroom material.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一句拉丁语「我看见」出发，这个词扩展成录像、信号、网络短片、动词与课堂材料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: moving pictures playing on a phone screen.
core.cn: 核心意象：手机屏幕上播放的活动画面。

branches.en: The recording branch: a self-introduction filmed at home.
branches.cn: 录像分支：家里录的自我介绍。

branches.en: The signal branch: a lecture sent by video.
branches.cn: 信号分支：靠视频传送的课。

branches.en: The feed branch: an hour of short clips.
branches.cn: 信息流分支：刷一小时的短片。

branches.en: The camera branch: filming the whole ceremony.
branches.cn: 镜头分支：录下整场仪式。

branches.en: The classroom branch: video added to a unit.
branches.cn: 课堂分支：单元里加入影像。
