intro.en: The Latin root vid-, vis- means to see; video is the bare verb form used as a noun.
intro.cn: 拉丁词根 vid-、vis- 意为看见，video 是直接用作名词的动词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre, to see, gives video, visible, vision, and television; the root appears whole in this word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre（看见）派生 video、visible、vision、television，本词中词根完整呈现。

items.exampleCN: vid- 在 video 中意为看见。
videotape 由 video 与 tape 合成。

items.example: Audio is the hearing partner of video.
items.exampleCN: audio 是 video 的听觉对应词。

definition_zh: 景色；看法；视野；观看
definition_en: what can be seen from a place, or the way a person thinks about something
core_image: 推开旅馆的窗，整片湖面铺在眼前
scene: 旅馆房间在六楼，她拉开窗帘，整片湖面就铺在眼前。The room has a fine view of the lake and the hills behind it.
sceneCN: 这里 view 是「景色」（第 1 个义项：从某处能看到的景象）；句意为这个房间能看到湖与湖后群山的好景色。推开窗后铺开的画面正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -er 构成，义为「观众；观看者」
合成词，义为「观点；视角」
加前缀 re- 构成，义为「回顾；评论」

senses.title: What can be seen from a place
senses.definition: the whole scene that a place allows you to see
senses.definitionCN: 从某一位置能看到的整体景象
senses.example: The room has a fine view of the lake and the hills behind it.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间能看到湖与湖后群山的好景色。
senses.why: To look out is to see; the scene laid before the eyes is the view.
senses.whyCN: 向外看是「看」这个动作，而铺在眼前的那片景象就是 view。

senses.title: A person’s opinion about something
senses.definition: a particular way of thinking about a matter
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的特定想法
senses.example: In my view the plan costs too much.
senses.exampleCN: 在我看来这个计划花费太高。
senses.why: The eye and the mind use one word: what you see from where you stand is what you think from where you stand.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛与头脑共用一个词：从哪个位置看，就从哪个位置想。

senses.title: The range within which something can be seen
senses.definition: the area that can be seen from a point, or the chance to see something
senses.definitionCN: 从一个位置能看见的区域，或看见某物的机会
senses.example: The ship came into view at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时那艘船出现在视野里。
senses.why: A view is not only the picture but the space in which the picture can appear.
senses.whyCN: view 不只是那幅画面，也是画面得以出现的空间。

senses.title: To look at something carefully
senses.definition: to watch or examine something, especially for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有目的地观看或检查某物
senses.example: The committee viewed the site before voting.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会在表决前察看了现场。
senses.why: The noun gives a verb: to give a thing your view is to view it.
senses.whyCN: 名词派生动词：把目光给某物，就是去观看它。

senses.title: To regard something in a certain way
senses.definition: to think of something as being a particular thing
senses.definitionCN: 把某物视为某一性质的事物
senses.example: Many people view silence as agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 很多人把沉默看作同意。
senses.why: When the mind places a thing before itself, the same verb names the judgment.
senses.whyCN: 当头脑把一物摆在自身之前端详时，这个动词也用来表示判断。

senses.title: What can be seen in a picture or on a screen
senses.definition: the scene shown in an image, drawing, or display
senses.definitionCN: 图像、图画或屏幕中显示的场景
senses.example: The drawing shows the house from the front view.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画从正面视角画了这座房子。
senses.why: Images repeat the word, naming the angle from which a scene is drawn.
senses.whyCN: 图像沿用了这个词，用来指画面取景的角度。

intro.en: View comes from Old French veue, a seeing, from Latin videre, to see.
intro.cn: view 来自古法语 veue（看见），源头是拉丁语 videre（看）。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and its past participle visus gave the noun of seeing.
items.cn: videre 意为看见，其过去分词 visus 派生出「所见」的名词。

items.en: French veue named the act of seeing and the sight itself.
items.cn: 法语 veue 既指看的动作，也指所见之物。

items.en: English borrowed it as vewe, later spelled view.
items.cn: 英语借入作 vewe，后来拼作 view。

items.en: The sense widened from sight to the scene before the eyes.
items.cn: 词义从「看」扩展到眼前的景象。

items.en: Opinion and examination joined the family, giving in my view and to view a site.
items.cn: 「看法」与「检查」加入词族，产生 in my view 与 view a site。

note.en: The first group holds words built on view, the second the words for scenes and opinions.
note.cn: 第一组是由 view 构成的词，第二组是表示景象与看法的词。

entries.definition: a person who watches
a position from which one thinks
to look over again
more than one opinion
a place as it looks
the power or act of seeing
what one thinks
a broad look over an area

normalIntro.en: Latin to see becomes both the thing seen and the thought held: the eye and the mind share one short word.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「看」既成为所见之物，也成为所持之见：眼睛与头脑共用一个短词。

normal.en: View is short but the vowel is long: /vjuː/.
normal.cn: view 拼写不长，但元音读长音 /vjuː/。

normal.en: Viewer adds -er for the one watching.
normal.cn: viewer 加 -er 表示观看的人。

normal.en: Viewpoint joins view and point, a place to think from.
normal.cn: viewpoint 由 view 与 point 合成，指思考所站的位置。

normal.en: Review begins with re-, to look again.
normal.cn: review 以 re- 开头，意为再看一遍。

normal.en: In my view is the standard way to give an opinion.
normal.cn: 给出看法时常用 in my view。

abstract.en: See curtains pulled back onto a wide lake.
abstract.cn: 想窗帘被拉开，露出一整片湖。

abstract.en: Picture two people on one hill looking different ways.
abstract.cn: 想一座山上两个人朝不同方向看。

abstract.en: Hear someone say that is how I see it.
abstract.cn: 听有人说，我就是这么看的。

examples.en: From the top of the tower the whole town is in view.
examples.cn: 从塔顶望去，整座小镇尽收眼底。

examples.en: The council viewed the plans with suspicion.
examples.cn: 议会带着怀疑看待这些计划。

examples.en: Her view of the matter changed after the meeting.
examples.cn: 会议之后，她对这件事的看法变了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「V 呦」——站在山顶比个 V，呦，风景真好看。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看见）→ 过去分词 visus → 古法语 veue → 英语 view

sensesIntro.en: The word starts with a scene from a window and ends with a judgment in the mind; the verb bridges watching and regarding.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从窗外的景象开始，走到心中的判断；动词则连接了「观看」与「看作」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lake spread out beyond an open window.
core.cn: 核心意象：敞开的窗外铺开一片湖。

branches.en: The window branch: lake and hills from a room.
branches.cn: 窗户分支：房里望见的湖与山。

branches.en: The opinion branch: my view on the cost.
branches.cn: 看法分支：我对花费的看法。

branches.en: The range branch: a ship heaving into sight.
branches.cn: 范围分支：船驶入视野。

branches.en: The looking branch: viewing a site, and viewing silence as consent.
branches.cn: 观看分支：察看现场，把沉默看作同意。

branches.en: The drawing branch: a house shown from the front view.
branches.cn: 绘图分支：房子的正面视图。

intro.en: The root vid-, vis-, view- means to see; -er, -point, and re- extend the word.
intro.cn: 词根 vid-、vis-、view- 意为看见，-er、-point、re- 扩展这个词。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre, to see, passed through French as veue and reaches English as view, with its relatives visible and vision.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre（看见）经法语 veue 传入英语成为 view，同族还有 visible 与 vision。

items.example: A viewpoint is where one stands to think.
items.exampleCN: viewpoint 是思考所站的位置。

items.example: Preview shows the work before release.
items.exampleCN: preview 在上映前展示作品。
visible 与词根 vis- 同源。

definition_zh: 村庄；村子；（统称）村民
definition_en: a small settlement in the countryside, smaller than a town
core_image: 山谷里几十间灰瓦房，一条路从村口穿过
scene: 地图上那一点很小，但走进去有小学、有杂货铺、有坐在门口的老人。The village has one school, one shop, and two hundred people.
sceneCN: 这里 village 是「村庄」（第 1 个义项：比城镇小的乡村聚落）；句意为这个村子有一所学校、一家店、两百口人。山谷里几十间灰瓦房的画面就是这个词的意思。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -er 构成，义为「村民」
villager 的复数，义为「村民们」
加 -like 构成，义为「村庄般的」

senses.title: A small country settlement
senses.definition: a small group of houses in the countryside
senses.definitionCN: 乡村中一小片房屋构成的聚落
senses.example: The village has one school, one shop, and two hundred people.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子有一所学校、一家店、两百口人。
senses.why: Latin villa was a country house, and a cluster of them became a village.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 villa 是乡间宅院，几座聚在一起就成了村庄。

senses.title: The people living there
senses.definition: the inhabitants of such a place, taken together
senses.definitionCN: 住在这样一个地方的人们，作为整体看
senses.example: The whole village came out to watch the parade.
senses.exampleCN: 全村人都出来看游行。
senses.why: Once houses stand together, the word can mean the people inside them.
senses.whyCN: 房屋一旦聚在一起，这个词就可以指住在里面的人。

senses.title: A district inside a city
senses.definition: a small area of a city that feels like a country village
senses.definitionCN: 城市里像乡村村庄的一小片区域
senses.example: Greenwich Village is famous for its small streets.
senses.exampleCN: 格林尼治村以其小街巷闻名。
senses.why: City planners borrowed the warm image of the country village for an urban quarter.
senses.whyCN: 城市规划者借用了乡村村庄的温暖意象来称呼城市街区。

senses.title: A settlement in a game or story
senses.definition: a small settlement used as a setting in games and fiction
senses.definitionCN: 游戏与虚构作品中作为场景的小聚落
senses.example: Players return to the village to trade supplies.
senses.exampleCN: 玩家回到村庄交换补给。
senses.why: Any small settlement in an imagined world takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 想象世界里的任何小聚落都沿用这个名字。

senses.title: The adjective use in names
senses.definition: used before another noun to describe something belonging to a village
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，表示属于村庄的
senses.example: Village life moves more slowly than city life.
senses.exampleCN: 乡村生活比城市生活节奏更慢。
senses.why: A settled place easily turns into a describing word.
senses.whyCN: 一个固定的地方很容易转成修饰用的词。

intro.en: Village grew from Latin villa, a country estate, through French into English.
intro.cn: village 从拉丁语 villa（乡间庄园）经法语进入英语。

items.en: Villa was a country house with land around it.
items.cn: villa 是带有周围土地的乡间宅邸。

items.en: Villaticus described what belonged to such an estate.
items.cn: villaticus 形容属于这种庄园的东西。

items.en: French village named the group of houses that grew near a villa.
items.cn: 法语 village 指在庄园附近发展起来的房屋群。

items.en: English village covered a small settlement with a church.
items.cn: 中世纪英语 village 指带教堂的小聚落。

items.en: The word later lent itself to city quarters and game settings.
items.cn: 后来这个词也被用于城市街区与游戏场景。

note.en: The first group holds the villa family, the second the nearby words for settlements.
note.cn: 第一组是 villa 词族，第二组是表示聚落的相近词。

entries.definition: a person who lives in a village
a large country house
the plural form
daily life in the countryside
a larger settlement with shops and offices
a very small group of houses
a place where people have settled
a large and busy urban place

normalIntro.en: A villa is one house; a village is the ring of houses that gathers around it.
normalIntro.cn: villa 是一座宅子，village 是围着它聚成的房群。

normal.en: Villa plus -age gives village, as in village of houses.
normal.cn: villa 加 -age 得 village，即一片房舍。

normal.en: Add -er for villager, the person; keep the g.
normal.cn: 加 -er 得 villager（村民），注意 g 保留。

normal.en: The plural adds -s to the whole word: villages.
normal.cn: 复数在整词后加 -s：villages。

normal.en: Think small: one school, one shop, one road.
normal.cn: 往小处想：一所学校、一家店、一条路。

normal.en: Greenwich Village shows the word used inside a city.
normal.cn: Greenwich Village 展示了城市内的用法。

abstract.en: See grey roofs in a valley with one road through.
abstract.cn: 想山谷里一片灰屋顶，一条路穿过。

abstract.en: Hear a bell that the whole valley can hear.
abstract.cn: 听一口全谷都听得见的钟。

abstract.en: Picture the old men at the doorway watching the road.
abstract.cn: 想老人们坐在门口望着那条路。

examples.en: They moved from the city to a small village.
examples.cn: 他们从城市搬到了一个小村庄。

examples.en: Every villager helped rebuild the bridge.
examples.cn: 每位村民都参与了修桥。

examples.en: The village is quiet except on market day.
examples.cn: 这个村子除了集市日都很安静。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为立志」——年轻人为了立志出山，把家乡的小村庄留在身后。

root: 拉丁语 villa（乡间庄园）→ 古法语 village → 中世纪英语 village

sensesIntro.en: One country estate grows into a cluster of houses, then into the people, then into a street of the big city.
sensesIntro.cn: 一座乡间庄园长成一片房舍，再长成住在里面的人，最后长成大城市里的一条街。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: grey roofs in a valley, one road through.
core.cn: 核心意象：山谷里的灰屋顶与一条穿村的路。

branches.en: The place branch: one school and two hundred people.
branches.cn: 地点分支：一所学校与两百个人。

branches.en: The people branch: the whole village at the parade.
branches.cn: 人物分支：全村的看游行的人。

branches.en: The city branch: small streets called a village.
branches.cn: 城市分支：被称为「村」的小街巷。

branches.en: The story branch: players trading in the village.
branches.cn: 故事分支：玩家在村里交易。

branches.en: The naming branch: village life in a report.
branches.cn: 命名分支：报道中的乡村生活。

intro.en: The stem vill- means a country estate; -age makes a collective noun, -er makes the person.
intro.cn: 词干 vill- 意为乡间庄园，-age 构成集合名词，-er 构成表人的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin villa gave French village and English village, with villager built on top.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 villa 派生法语 village 与英语 village，再由此构成 villager。

items.example: Vill- points to a house in the fields.
items.exampleCN: vill- 指向田野中的宅子。

items.example: Village is a group of villas.
A villager lives in the village.
A villagelike street in the old town.
items.exampleCN: 老城里一条像村庄的街。

items.example: A village grows into a town.
They rented a villa by the sea.
items.exampleCN: 他们在海边租了一栋别墅。

items.example: A village inside a city is a neighbourhood.

definition_zh: 暴力；暴行；猛烈
definition_en: behaviour meant to hurt or kill people, or great force in nature or feeling
core_image: 街角围起的人群，地上散落的碎玻璃
scene: 深夜的街角围起了警戒线，地上散着碎玻璃，警察在记录现场。The city has seen a rise in violence since the summer.
sceneCN: 这里 violence 是「暴力」（第 1 个义项：意图伤害或杀害他人的行为）；句意为入夏以来这座城市的暴力事件增多了。街角围着的人群与碎玻璃正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 同源形容词，义为「暴力的；猛烈的」
加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「猛烈地」
同源动词，义为「违反；侵犯」

senses.title: Behaviour meant to hurt people
senses.definition: actions intended to injure, damage, or kill
senses.definitionCN: 意图伤害、破坏或杀害他人的行为
senses.example: The city has seen a rise in violence since the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 入夏以来这座城市的暴力事件增多了。
senses.why: From Latin violentia, the word names force pushed to the point of harm.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自拉丁语 violentia，指被推到伤害程度的力量。

senses.title: Great force in nature
senses.definition: the destructive power of storms, earthquakes, or other natural forces
senses.definitionCN: 风暴、地震等自然力量造成的破坏力
senses.example: The violence of the storm tore roofs from houses.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴之猛把房顶都掀了下来。
senses.why: Nature uses no fists, yet a storm’s force is spoken of with the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 自然并没有拳头，但风暴的力量用的仍是这个词。

senses.title: Intensity of feeling or expression
senses.definition: extreme force in emotion, words, or action
senses.definitionCN: 情感、言辞或行为上的极端强度
senses.example: She spoke with a violence that surprised her friends.
senses.exampleCN: 她说话之激烈让朋友们吃了一惊。
senses.why: Feelings can press as hard as hands, so intensity of speech borrows the word of blows.
senses.whyCN: 情绪能像手一样用力，于是言语的激烈借用了拳头的说法。

senses.title: Unlawful force in law
senses.definition: the use of physical force against a person or property contrary to law
senses.definitionCN: 对人身或财产非法使用的物理强制
senses.example: The charge was robbery with violence.
senses.exampleCN: 罪名是暴力抢劫。
senses.why: Courts need a precise term for force that breaks the law, and violence supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 法院需要一个精确术语指违法的强制，violence 正好胜任。

senses.title: In media, images of fighting and cruelty
senses.definition: shown fighting, killing, or cruelty in films and games
senses.definitionCN: 影视与游戏中展示的打斗、杀戮或残忍
senses.example: Parents asked for less violence in the evening schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 家长要求在晚间节目里少放暴力内容。
senses.why: Once screens show the act, the noun names the content as well as the deed.
senses.whyCN: 屏幕一旦展示这种行为，这个词既指行为，也指内容。

intro.en: Violence goes back to Latin violentia, from vis, force.
intro.cn: violence 追溯至拉丁语 violentia，源自 vis（力量）。

items.en: Vis meant force or power, and violentia named the quality of using it hard.
items.cn: vis 意为力量或强力，violentia 指蛮横使用力量的性质。

items.en: Violare, to treat with force, shares the same root.
items.cn: violare（施暴、亵渎）与它同根。

items.en: French violence carried the noun into English law and letters.
items.cn: 法语 violence 把这一名词带进英语的法律与文章。

items.en: English used it first for unlawful force.
items.cn: 中世纪英语先用它指非法强制。

items.en: Storms, feelings, and screen content took the word far beyond the courtroom.
items.cn: 风暴、情感与屏幕内容把这个词带出了法庭。

note.en: The first group holds the violence family, the second the words for force, fighting, and calm.
note.cn: 第一组是 violence 词族，第二组是力量、打斗与平静的相关词。

entries.definition: using force to hurt
with great force
to break or invade
the act of breaking a rule
strength used on a person or thing
cruel and savage treatment
a serious disagreement or fight
the absence of fighting

normalIntro.en: The root vis, force, fills the word: violence is force taken too far.
normalIntro.cn: 词根 vis（力量）贯穿全词：暴力就是把力量用过了头。

normal.en: Violet and violence look alike; only the ending differs.
normal.cn: violet 与 violence 形近，只差词尾。

normal.en: Violence ends in -ence, like patience.
normal.cn: violence 以 -ence 结尾，如同 patience。

normal.en: The adjective drops -nce for -nt: violent.
normal.cn: 形容词把 -nce 换成 -nt：violent。

normal.en: Resort to violence is a fixed phrase for turning to force.
normal.cn: 诉诸暴力常说 resort to violence。

normal.en: The stress falls on the first syllable: VI-o-lence.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节：VI-o-lence。

abstract.en: See broken glass on a corner at night.
abstract.cn: 想夜里街角的碎玻璃。

abstract.en: Hear a window shake as the storm hits.
abstract.cn: 听风暴来时的窗玻璃作响。

abstract.en: Picture a hand clenched over a table.
abstract.cn: 想桌子上一只攥紧的手。

examples.en: The report calls for an end to violence in the home.
examples.cn: 这份报告呼吁终止家庭暴力。

examples.en: No cause justifies the use of violence.
examples.cn: 任何理由都不能为使用暴力开脱。

examples.en: The violence of the waves kept the boats in port.
examples.cn: 浪势太猛，船都留在了港里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外来冷死」——外来的人被打得冷死在街头，这桩暴力令人心惊。

root: 拉丁语 vis（力量）→ violentia（强暴）→ 古法语 violence → 英语 violence

sensesIntro.en: Force used against people becomes the force of storms, of speech, of law, and of what screens show.
sensesIntro.cn: 用在人身上的力量，进而变成风暴之力、言语之力、法律上的强制与屏幕上的内容。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a police line around broken glass at night.
core.cn: 核心意象：夜里警戒线围住的碎玻璃。

branches.en: The street branch: more attacks since summer.
branches.cn: 街头分支：入夏后袭击增多。

branches.en: The storm branch: roofs torn away.
branches.cn: 风暴分支：房顶被掀掉。

branches.en: The voice branch: a tone that startles friends.
branches.cn: 语气分支：让朋友吃惊的激烈语调。

branches.en: The court branch: a charge of robbery with force.
branches.cn: 法庭分支：暴力抢劫的罪名。

branches.en: The screen branch: parents ask for less of it.
branches.cn: 屏幕分支：家长要求少放暴力。

intro.en: The root viol-, from Latin vis, force, builds violence, violent, violate, and violation.
intro.cn: 词根 viol- 源自拉丁语 vis（力量），构成 violence、violent、violate、violation。

latinIntro.en: Latin vis, force, gives violentia; the -ence ending marks an abstract noun, as in patience.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vis（力量）派生 violentia；-ence 词尾标记抽象名词，如同 patience。

items.example: Viol- carries the sense of force.
Violence names the state of using force.
items.exampleCN: violence 指使用力量的状态。

items.example: Violate means to break with force.
A violation of the rule was reported.
items.exampleCN: 有人举报了违反规则之事。

items.example: Force is the plain word behind vis.

和平正是暴力所破坏的。

definition_zh: 暴力的；猛烈的；剧烈的
definition_en: using or involving force meant to hurt, or happening with great force
core_image: 被人一把推开的门，撞在墙上反弹回来
scene: 电影里两个人争执起来，其中一个一把把桌子掀翻，杯子全摔在地上。The argument turned violent before anyone could stop it.
sceneCN: 这里 violent 是「暴力的」（第 1 个义项：涉及意在伤害他人的武力）；句意为还没人来得及阻止，争吵就演变成暴力冲突。被掀翻的桌子与砸碎的杯子正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 去后缀 -ent 构成的名词，义为「暴力」
加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「猛烈地」
加前缀 non- 构成，义为「非暴力的」

senses.title: Using force to hurt people
senses.definition: using physical force intended to injure or kill
senses.definitionCN: 使用意在伤害或杀害他人的体力
senses.example: The argument turned violent before anyone could stop it.
senses.exampleCN: 还没人来得及阻止，争吵就演变成了暴力冲突。
senses.why: A violent act is force aimed at a body, and the sentence usually shows a body receiving it.
senses.whyCN: 暴力行为是针对人体施加的力量，句子里往往能看到承受的那具身体。

senses.title: Happening with great natural force
senses.definition: of weather or natural events, striking with great power
senses.definitionCN: 天气或自然现象以巨大力量袭来
senses.example: A violent storm closed the harbour for two days.
senses.exampleCN: 一场猛烈的风暴让港口停摆两天。
senses.why: Nature strikes with the same force as a fist, so the adjective crosses over.
senses.whyCN: 自然的力量与拳头一样，形容词因此跨了过来。

senses.title: Extremely strong in feeling
senses.definition: of feelings, reactions, or changes, very strong and sudden
senses.definitionCN: 指情感、反应或变化非常强烈而突然
senses.example: He had a violent dislike of being interrupted.
senses.exampleCN: 他极其厌恶被人打断。
senses.why: A feeling that arrives with force takes the adjective of force, even without any blow.
senses.whyCN: 猛然涌来的情绪也用了表示力量的那个形容词，即便没有任何一击。

senses.title: In law, involving force against a person
senses.definition: of a crime, committed with force against a person
senses.definitionCN: 指犯罪时对人使用了强制
senses.example: He was charged with violent robbery.
senses.exampleCN: 他被控暴力抢劫。
senses.why: Law separates crimes with force from those without, and the adjective does that work.
senses.whyCN: 法律把带强制的犯罪与不带强制的分开，这个形容词正承担这一区分。

senses.title: In colour or light, very intense
senses.definition: of colour, extremely bright and harsh to the eye
senses.definitionCN: 指颜色极其鲜明、刺眼
senses.example: A violent orange covered the whole wall.
senses.exampleCN: 整面墙刷成了刺眼的橘色。
senses.why: Strong colour hits the eye the way a blow hits the body, so the sense extends.
senses.whyCN: 强烈的颜色冲击眼睛，如同打击冲击身体，词义由此延伸。

intro.en: Violent comes from Latin violentia, the quality of force.
intro.cn: violent 来自拉丁语 violentia，指力量的性质。

items.en: Vis was force, and violentus described one full of it.
items.cn: vis 是力量，violentus 形容充满力量的人。

items.en: The adjective came before the English noun, both from the same stem.
items.cn: 形容词先于英语名词出现，二者同出一词干。

items.en: French violent passed the adjective into English.
items.cn: 法语 violent 把形容词传入英语。

items.en: English used it for blows, storms, and heated speech.
items.cn: 中世纪英语用它指打击、风暴与激烈的言辞。

items.en: Colour and reaction senses joined in later centuries.
items.cn: 色彩与反应等义项在之后的世纪加入。

note.en: The first group holds the violent family, the second the adjectives for force, rage, and calm.
note.cn: 第一组是 violent 词族，第二组是力量、愤怒与平静的形容词。

normalIntro.en: The ending -ent marks the adjective; the stem marks the force.
normalIntro.cn: 词尾 -ent 标记形容词，词干标记力量。

normal.en: Drop -ent and add -ence for the noun violence.
normal.cn: 去掉 -ent 加 -ence 得名词 violence。

normal.en: Add -ly for violently, with force in the manner.
normal.cn: 加 -ly 得 violently，表示方式猛烈。

normal.en: Nonviolent puts non- in front to deny the force.

normal.en: Compare with more violent, not violenter.

normal.en: The second syllable is weak: VI-o-lent.

examples.en: The crowd grew violent after the refused request.
examples.cn: 请求被拒之后人群动起手来。

examples.en: A violent wind tore the sails in minutes.
examples.cn: 一阵狂风几分钟就把帆撕破了。

examples.en: Her violent reaction showed how much the news hurt.
examples.cn: 她激烈的反应说明这消息伤她多深。

sensesIntro.en: Force aimed at people, storms, feelings, crimes, and even paint share one adjective.
sensesIntro.cn: 针对人的力量、风暴、情绪、罪名，甚至油漆，共用同一个形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door flung so hard it bounces off the wall.

intro.en: Violent shares the stem viol- with violence and violate; -ent makes it an adjective.
intro.cn: violent 与 violence、violate 共用词干 viol-，-ent 使其成为形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin violentus described what is full of vis, force; the ending -ent means having that quality.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 violentus 形容充满 vis（力量）之物，-ent 意为具有该性质。

items.example: Viol- is the force in violent.
items.exampleCN: viol- 是 violent 中的力量。

definition_zh: 几乎；实际上；虚拟地
definition_en: almost entirely, or in effect, or by means of a computer simulation
core_image: 一间空荡荡的教室，屏幕上却坐满了人
scene: 考试前一周，老师发现班里的座位几乎空了一半，学生都在线上听课。Virtually every student had watched the lecture online before the test.
sceneCN: 这里 virtually 是「几乎、差不多」（第 1 个义项：接近全部但未绝对如此）；句意为考试前几乎每个学生都在网上看过这节课。空了一半的教室正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 去后缀 -ly 构成的形容词，义为「实质上的；虚拟的」
同源名词，义为「美德；优点」
加后缀 -ize 构成，义为「虚拟化」

senses.title: Almost, for practical purposes
senses.definition: almost completely, with only a very small exception
senses.definitionCN: 几乎完全如此，只有极小的例外
senses.example: Virtually every student had watched the lecture online before the test.
senses.exampleCN: 考试前几乎每个学生都在网上看过这节课。
senses.why: From virtue in the old sense of power or effect: what holds in effect holds almost everywhere.
senses.whyCN: 源自古义为「效力」的 virtue：在效力上成立的，就几乎处处成立。

senses.title: In effect, though not in name
senses.definition: in practice or in effect, even if not formally so
senses.definitionCN: 实际上如此，尽管名义上并非如此
senses.example: The two plans are virtually the same.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个计划实际上是一样的。
senses.why: When a difference exists only on paper, the adverb says the effect is the same.
senses.whyCN: 当差别只存在于纸面上时，这个副词就说明效果相同。

senses.title: By computer simulation
senses.definition: by means of a computer model or online environment rather than in person
senses.definitionCN: 通过计算机模型或网络环境而非实体方式
senses.example: The whole factory was tested virtually before it was built.
senses.exampleCN: 整座工厂在建造前先做了虚拟测试。
senses.why: Modern computing gave virtual a new sense, and the adverb followed it into the lab.
senses.whyCN: 现代计算给了 virtual 新义，副词也随它走进了实验室。

senses.title: By remote or online means
senses.definition: through online channels instead of a physical place
senses.definitionCN: 通过线上渠道而非实体场所
senses.example: Half the team works virtually from other cities.
senses.exampleCN: 团队一半的人在其他城市远程工作。
senses.why: A meeting held on screens is held in effect, so the adverb covers remote work.
senses.whyCN: 在屏幕上开的会实际上也是会，副词因此也涵盖远程工作。

senses.title: Nearly, but not quite
senses.definition: close to a state without reaching it fully
senses.definitionCN: 接近某状态但尚未完全达到
senses.example: The old road is virtually gone under the new houses.
senses.exampleCN: 那条老路在新房子下几乎不见了。
senses.why: The word keeps a small door open, since virtually stops short of completely.
senses.whyCN: 这个词始终留着一道小门，因为 virtually 并不等于 completely。

intro.en: Virtually is virtual plus -ly; virtual comes from virtue, once meaning power or effect.
intro.cn: virtually 是 virtual 加 -ly；virtual 来自 virtue，古义为力量、效力。

items.en: Virtus meant worth, courage, and power, from vir, a man.
items.cn: virtus 意为价值、勇气与力量，源自 vir（男子）。

items.en: French vertu kept the sense of power or efficacy.
items.cn: 法语 vertu 保留了「力量、效力」之义。

items.en: English virtue covered moral worth and also active power.
items.cn: 中世纪英语的 virtue 兼指德行与实效力。

items.en: Virtual, and then virtually, meant effective in practice though not in name.
items.cn: virtual 及 virtually 表示名义上不是而实际上有效。

items.en: Computing added the sense of simulated by machine.
items.cn: 计算技术增加了「由机器模拟」之义。

note.en: The first group holds the virtual family, the second the adverbs of nearness and reality.
note.cn: 第一组是 virtual 词族，第二组是表示「近乎」与「实际」的副词。

normalIntro.en: Power in the old sense became effect in practice, and then the world seen on screens.
normalIntro.cn: 古义的力量变成实际效力，再变成屏幕上所见的那个世界。

normal.en: Virtual plus -ly gives the adverb; nothing changes in the stem.
normal.cn: virtual 加 -ly 即副词，词干不变。

normal.en: Virtually every goes together in reports and studies.
normal.cn: 报告与研究里常用 virtually every。

normal.en: Virtually is not exactly: the door to completely stays ajar.
normal.cn: virtually 并不等于 exactly，通往 completely 的门没全关。

normal.en: The word starts with virtue, not with virus.
normal.cn: 这个词开头是 virtue，不是 virus。

normal.en: The stress falls on the first syllable: VIR-tu-al-ly.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节：VIR-tu-al-ly。

abstract.en: See half-empty seats and lit screens.
abstract.cn: 想一半空着的座位与亮着的屏幕。

abstract.en: Picture a factory tested in a model first.
abstract.cn: 想工厂先在模型里被检验一遍。

abstract.en: Hear a voice on a headset saying it is almost done.
abstract.cn: 听耳机里的声音说差不多完成了。

examples.cn: 大雪几乎把这座小镇与外界隔绝。

examples.en: Virtually all the tickets were sold by noon.
examples.cn: 几乎所有票在中午前就卖光了。

examples.en: They met virtually for the first three months.
examples.cn: 头三个月他们都是线上见面。

root: 拉丁语 vir（男子）→ virtus（价值、力量）→ 古法语 vertu → virtue → virtual + -ly → virtually

sensesIntro.en: One adverb says almost, says in effect, and says through a screen: three ways of nearly being true.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个副词既说「几乎」，也说「实际上」，还说「隔着屏幕」，都是「近乎成真」的三种方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: empty seats, screens filled with faces.
core.cn: 核心意象：空座位与坐满屏幕的人脸。

branches.en: The almost branch: nearly every student, nearly the same, nearly gone.
branches.cn: 近乎分支：几乎每个学生、几乎一样、几乎消失。

branches.en: The effect branch: two plans alike in practice.
branches.cn: 效力分支：两个计划实际一样。

branches.en: The model branch: a factory tested on a computer.
branches.cn: 模型分支：在计算机里测试的工厂。

branches.en: The remote branch: a team spread across cities.
branches.cn: 远程分支：分散在各地办公的团队。

branches.en: The old road branch: a path lost under houses.
branches.cn: 老路分支：被房屋盖掉的路。

intro.en: The stem virt- means worth or power; -ual makes the adjective and -ly the adverb.
intro.cn: 词干 virt- 意为价值或力量，-ual 构成形容词，-ly 构成副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin virtus, from vir, man, meant worth and power; English virtual turned power into practical effect, and computing turned effect into simulation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 virtus（源自 vir「男子」）意为价值与力量；英语 virtual 把力量转为实际效力，计算技术又把效力转为模拟。

items.example: Virt- holds the sense of power.
Virtual means having the power in effect.
items.exampleCN: virtual 意为在效力上具备。

items.example: Virtually says it holds in effect.
items.exampleCN: virtually 表示在效果上成立。

items.example: Vir is the oldest link in the chain.
items.exampleCN: vir 是这条链上最早的环节。
practically 与 virtually 意义交叠。
virtually 不到 completely 的程度。

definition_zh: 美德；德行；优点；长处；效力；贞操
definition_en: a good quality of character, or a useful strength in a thing
core_image: 一个人把力气用在正处，站得笔直
scene: 毕业典礼上，老校长没有讲成绩，只讲了诚实与耐心这两件事。Patience was the one virtue the job truly required.
sceneCN: 这里 virtue 是「美德」（第 1 个义项：品格中的善）；句意为耐心是这份工作真正需要的一种美德。把力气用在正处、站得笔直的那个人，就是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 美德；德行；优点；长处；效力

collocations.zh: 化不得已为美德；将就办事

derivatives.zh: virtue 加 -ous 构成，义为「有德行的；正直的」
同出拉丁词根 virtus，义为「几乎；实际上」
同根形容词，义为「实质上的；虚拟的」
同根名词，义为「精湛技艺」

senses.title: A good quality of character
senses.definition: a quality in a person that is good and worth praising, such as honesty or courage
senses.definitionCN: 个人身上值得赞许的善的品质，如诚实、勇气
senses.example: Patience was the one virtue the job truly required.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是这份工作真正需要的一种美德。
senses.why: Latin virtus first meant manly strength and courage, and the word slowly moved from strength of body to strength of character used well.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 virtus 最初意为男子气概的力量与勇气，这个词慢慢从身体之力转到用得其所的品格之力。

senses.title: A good point in a thing
senses.definition: a useful strength or good feature in an object, a plan or a method
senses.definitionCN: 物体、方案或方法中可取的长处
senses.example: The chief virtue of the old car is that it never breaks down.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆旧车最大的优点是它从不坏。
senses.why: If a person can have good qualities, so can a plan; the word applies to anything with strengths worth naming.
senses.whyCN: 人能有好品质，方案也能，于是这个词用于任何值得称道的长处。

senses.title: Power to produce an effect
senses.definition: the power of something, such as a medicine or a herb, to act as it should
senses.definitionCN: 药物或草药等发挥应有作用的力量
senses.example: The virtue of the plant lies in its bitter root.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物的效力在于它苦涩的根。
senses.why: Older medicine spoke of the virtue of a herb, meaning its active strength, which is strength again, now inside a plant.
senses.whyCN: 早期医学讲草药的 virtue，指它的有效之力，还是「力量」，只是转到了植物身上。

senses.title: Chastity, especially of a woman
senses.definition: in older use, chastity, chiefly spoken of a woman
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法，指贞洁，主要用来指女性
senses.example: The old play makes her virtue a matter of public talk.
senses.exampleCN: 那部老戏把她的贞洁写成众人议论的事。
senses.why: A narrow set of rules once gathered around the word, so one particular virtue became the virtue; modern use keeps it mainly historical.
senses.whyCN: 一套狭窄的规矩曾围着这个词，于是某一种美德就成了 the virtue；现代用法主要保留历史色彩。

senses.title: Strength shown in a fixed phrase
senses.definition: in the fixed phrases by virtue of and in virtue of, meaning because of or through
senses.definitionCN: 固定短语 by virtue of、in virtue of 中，意为凭借、由于
senses.example: She entered by virtue of her father's old pass.
senses.exampleCN: 她凭父亲旧日的通行证进去了。
senses.why: To act by virtue of something is to act on the strength given by it, so the old sense of power survives in this phrase.
senses.whyCN: by virtue of 某物行事，就是借它给的力量行事，旧有的「力量」义在这个短语里活了下来。

intro.en: Virtue comes from Latin virtus, strength or manliness, from vir, a man.
intro.cn: virtue 来自拉丁语 virtus（力量、男子气），源自 vir（男人）。

items.en: Vir meant a man, and virtus named the strength and courage expected of one.
items.cn: vir 意为男人，virtus 指男人应有的力量与勇气。

items.en: Cicero and others widened virtus to cover moral excellence of any kind.
items.cn: 西塞罗等人把 virtus 扩展到各种道德上的优秀。

items.en: Old French vertu carried the moral sense into English.
items.cn: 古法语 vertu 把道德义带进英语。

items.en: English added the sense of a good point in a thing and of the active power of a herb or stone.
items.cn: 英语又添上事物的长处，以及草药或石头的效力。

items.en: By virtue of keeps the older sense of power, and virtual grew beside it with a sense of what works in effect.
items.cn: by virtue of 保留了较旧的「力量」义，virtual 在旁边长出「实际起效」的意思。

note.en: The first group holds the same-root family, the second the words for goodness and for a good point.
note.cn: 第一组收同根词族，第二组收表示善与优点的词。

entries.definition: The plural of the noun.
An adjective meaning having or showing moral goodness.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有德行的、正直的」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning acting in effect, though not in name or fact.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「实际起作用的、虚拟的」。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning almost, or in practice.
The quality of deserving praise, or a good point.
entries.definitionCN: 值得赞许之处，也指优点。

entries.definition: The general quality of being good.
The strengths of a case or a plan.
A bad habit or fault, the opposite of a virtue.

normalIntro.en: A word for manly strength became a word for moral strength, then for any useful strength.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示男子之力的词，先变成道德之力，再变成任何可用的长处。

normal.en: Virtue comes from vir, a man, and virtus, the strength expected of him.
normal.cn: virtue 来自 vir（男人）与 virtus（他应有的力量）。

normal.en: By virtue of means because of, and keeps the old sense of power.
normal.cn: by virtue of 意为由于，保留着旧的「力量」义。

normal.en: Virtue is a good quality in a person; a virtue can also be a good point in a plan.
normal.cn: virtue 是人的好品质，也可指方案的长处。

normal.en: The plural is virtues; the adjective is virtuous.
normal.cn: 复数是 virtues，形容词是 virtuous。

normal.en: Vice is the opposite of virtue.
normal.cn: vice 是 virtue 的反面。

abstract.en: See a person standing straight with strength used for something good.
abstract.cn: 想象一人站得笔直，把力气用在正处。

abstract.en: Hear a teacher praising honesty instead of marks.
abstract.cn: 听老师不提分数，只夸诚实。

abstract.en: Feel the silent working power inside a bitter herb.
abstract.cn: 感受苦草根里那股无言的作用之力。

examples.en: Honesty is a virtue he never had to learn.
examples.cn: 诚实是他不必去学的一种美德。

examples.en: They chose the small hotel for the virtue of its quiet garden.
examples.cn: 他们选这家小旅馆，是因为它有安静花园这个优点。

examples.en: He was admitted by virtue of a special licence.
examples.cn: 他凭一张特别许可得以进入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我求」——我求的是好品德，不是好分数。

root: 拉丁语 vir（男人）→ virtus（力量、勇气、美德）→ 古法语 vertu → 英语 virtue。

sensesIntro.en: Strength narrows to moral strength, then widens to a good point in a thing, to the power in a plant, and to a narrow historical sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 「力量」先缩成道德之力，再扩到事物的长处、植物的效力，以及一个狭窄的历史义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: strength held upright and used for good.
core.cn: 核心意象：站得笔直、用在正处的力量。

branches.en: The character branch: patience on the job.
branches.cn: 品格分支：工作所需的耐心。

branches.en: The good-point branch: a car that never breaks down.
branches.cn: 长处分支：从不坏的旧车。

branches.en: The power branch: a bitter root that works.
branches.cn: 效力分支：起作用的苦根。

branches.en: The historical branch: an old play about a woman's honour.
branches.cn: 历史分支：老戏里的名声。

branches.en: The phrase branch: entering by virtue of a pass.
branches.cn: 短语分支：凭通行证进入。

intro.en: Virt- comes from vir, a man; -ue arrived through French, and -ous, -ual, -ually build the family.
intro.cn: virt- 来自 vir（男人），-ue 经法语而来，-ous、-ual、-ually 撑起词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vir and virtus are both recorded, and virtus is common in classical prose.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vir 与 virtus 均有记录，virtus 在古典散文里很常见。

items.example: The noun is the root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族的词根。

items.example: The noun first meant manly strength.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词最初指男子之力。

definition_zh: 病毒；病毒性疾病；（计算机）病毒；恶毒影响
definition_en: a tiny agent that lives inside cells and makes copies of itself, often causing disease
core_image: 一个带刺的小球贴在细胞门口，正准备钻进去复制自己
scene: 一月的急诊室里，孩子的体温降不下来，医生先排除了细菌。The doctor said a virus, not bacteria, was causing the fever.
sceneCN: 这里 virus 是「病毒」（第 1 个义项：寄生在细胞里、复制自身并能致病的微小因子）；句意为医生说引起发热的是病毒而非细菌。贴到细胞门口的那个带刺小球，正是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 病毒；病毒性疾病；（电脑）病毒；恶毒影响

derivatives.zh: 由 virus 加 -al 构成，义为「病毒的； viral 式的」
vir 与 -ology 复合，义为「病毒学」
加 -ist 构成，义为「病毒学家」
同出拉丁词根，义为「剧毒的；恶毒的」

senses.title: A tiny disease agent
senses.definition: an infective agent too small to be seen under a normal microscope, multiplying only inside living cells
senses.definitionCN: 小到普通显微镜看不见，只能在活细胞内复制繁殖的感染因子
senses.example: The doctor said a virus, not bacteria, was causing the fever.
senses.exampleCN: 医生说引起发热的是病毒而非细菌。
senses.why: Latin virus meant poison or slime, and when scientists found an agent smaller than bacteria they gave it that old name.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 virus 意为毒液、黏液，科学家发现一种比细菌更小的因子时，就给它用了这个旧名。

senses.title: An illness caused by it
senses.definition: in everyday speech, a sickness thought to come from such an agent
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指由这类因子引起的病
senses.example: He has been off work for a week with a virus.
senses.exampleCN: 他因为一次病毒感染病休了一周。
senses.why: People name the illness after its cause, so a viral cold is simply called a virus.
senses.whyCN: 人们以病因称呼疾病，病毒性感冒就被直接叫作 a virus。

senses.title: A program that spreads itself
senses.definition: a hidden program that copies itself into other programs and damages them
senses.definitionCN: 能把自己复制到别的程序中、并造成破坏的隐藏程序
senses.example: The old laptop was slow because of a virus.
senses.exampleCN: 那台旧笔记本因为中了病毒而变慢。
senses.why: A computer virus spreads and multiplies like the biological one, so the borrowed name needed no change.
senses.whyCN: 电脑病毒像生物病毒一样传播、复制，借来的名字不必改动。

senses.title: A harmful influence
senses.definition: in literary use, something that corrupts a mind or a society
senses.definitionCN: 文学用法中指腐蚀人心或社会的东西
senses.example: The writer called envy a virus of the mind.
senses.exampleCN: 那位作家把嫉妒称为精神上的病毒。
senses.why: Poison spreading unseen is an old image for bad influence, which explains the literary sense.
senses.whyCN: 看不见地扩散的毒，是描述恶劣影响的旧意象，文学义由此而来。

senses.title: Poison in the old sense
senses.definition: in Latin and early English, a poisonous liquid or a foul humour
senses.definitionCN: 在拉丁语与早期英语里指毒液或有毒的体液
senses.example: Old medicine blamed a virus in the blood for the swelling.
senses.exampleCN: 早期医学把这种肿痛归咎于血液中的毒。
senses.why: Before viruses were seen, the word named any poison, and trace of that sense survives in virulent.
senses.whyCN: 在病毒被看见之前，这个词泛指任何毒，这层意思还留在 virulent 里。

intro.en: Virus is Latin for poison or slime, and science borrowed it as a technical term only in modern times.
intro.cn: virus 在拉丁语里指毒液或黏液，科学界只是在近代才把它借作术语。

items.en: Virus meant a poisonous liquid, slime or a foul discharge.
items.cn: virus 意为毒液、黏液或恶臭的分泌物。

items.en: English used it for poison in the seventeenth century, mostly in scientific writing.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪用它表示毒，主要用于科学写作。

items.en: After filters caught bacteria but not the smaller agent, virus was used for the new class.
items.cn: 过滤器能拦住细菌却拦不住更小的因子后，virus 被用来指这一新类别。

items.en: Electron microscopes made the particles visible in the nineteen thirties.
items.cn: 三十年代的电子显微镜使这些颗粒变得可见。

items.en: Computer use in the nineteen seventies and the adjective viral in the internet age added new branches.
items.cn: 七十年代的电脑用法与互联网时代的形容词 viral 又添了新枝。

note.en: The first group follows the family and the look-alike, the second the words for germs and their effects.
note.cn: 第一组收同族词与形近词，第二组收病菌及其影响类词。

entries.definition: The plural form of the noun.
An adjective meaning of a virus, or spreading fast online.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「病毒的、在网上迅速传播的」。

entries.definition: The scientific study of viruses.
An adjective from the same Latin root meaning very poisonous or bitter.
entries.definitionCN: 同根形容词，义为「剧毒的、恶毒的」。

entries.definition: Single-celled organisms that can also cause disease, larger than viruses.
entries.definitionCN: 单细胞生物，也能致病，比病毒大。

entries.definition: An everyday word for any microbe that spreads disease.
entries.definitionCN: 日常用词，泛指致病微生物。

entries.definition: The condition caused when an agent enters the body.
entries.definitionCN: 病原进入身体后造成的状况。

entries.definition: An adjective for diseases spread from person to person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，形容疾病在人际传播。

normalIntro.en: One Latin word for poison serves a microbe, a sickness, a program and a bad idea.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁的「毒」字，同时服务微生物、一场病、一个程序与一个坏念头。

normal.en: Virus and virulent share a Latin root meaning poison.
normal.cn: virus 与 virulent 同出拉丁「毒」字词根。

normal.en: The plural is viruses; the adjective is viral.
normal.cn: 复数是 viruses，形容词是 viral。

normal.en: A virus needs a living cell; bacteria do not.
normal.cn: 病毒需要活细胞，细菌不需要。

normal.en: A computer virus copies itself into other programs, just as the biological one does.
normal.cn: 电脑病毒如生物病毒一样把自己复制进别的程序。

normal.en: Viral also means spreading fast on the internet.
normal.cn: viral 还指在网上迅速传播。

abstract.en: See a spiky ball landing on a cell wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一个带刺小球落在细胞壁上。

abstract.en: Hear a doctor say it is a virus, so an antibiotic will not help.
abstract.cn: 听医生说这是病毒，抗生素没用。

abstract.en: Picture a line of code quietly copying itself into a file.
abstract.cn: 想象一行代码悄悄把自己复制进一个文件。

examples.en: A virus cannot multiply without a living cell.
examples.cn: 病毒没有活细胞就不能繁殖。

examples.en: Most winter viruses spread through the air.
examples.cn: 多数冬季病毒通过空气传播。

examples.en: He lost all his files to a virus.
examples.cn: 一次病毒让他的文件全丢了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪螺」——长得歪歪扭扭的螺丝状小球，专往细胞里钻。

root: 拉丁语 virus（毒液、黏液）→ 科学拉丁语 virus（病毒）→ 英语 virus；同根词有 virulent。

sensesIntro.en: A Latin word for poison ends up meaning the smallest cause of illness, then the illness, then a program, then a harmful idea.
sensesIntro.cn: 拉丁的「毒」先是变成最小的病因，再变成那场病、那个程序，最后变成一个有害念头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spiked particle landing on a cell.
core.cn: 核心意象：落在细胞上的带刺颗粒。

branches.en: The agent branch: a virus rather than bacteria.
branches.cn: 病原分支：是病毒而非细菌。

branches.en: The illness branch: off work for a week with a virus.
branches.cn: 疾病分支：因病毒感染病休一周。

branches.en: The computer branch: a laptop slowed by a virus.
branches.cn: 电脑分支：被病毒弄慢的笔记本。

branches.en: The metaphor branch: envy as a virus of the mind.
branches.cn: 比喻分支：嫉妒是精神的病毒。

branches.en: The old branch: a poison in the blood.
branches.cn: 旧义分支：血中的毒。

intro.en: Vir- carries the Latin poison; -us was the Latin ending, and -al, -ology, -ist build modern words.
intro.cn: vir- 携带拉丁的「毒」，-us 是拉丁词尾，-al、-ology、-ist 搭出现代词。

latinIntro.en: Latin virus is recorded for a poison or a slime; the adjective virulentus is also recorded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 virus 有毒液、黏液义都有记录，形容词 virulentus 同样有记录。

items.example: The root carries the idea of poison.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根携带「毒」的意思。

items.example: The noun is Latin, not a coinage.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是拉丁词，不是新造词。

items.example: The ending stayed in Latin form.
items.exampleCN: 该词尾保留了拉丁形式。

definition_zh: 看得见的；可见的；明显的；显而易见的
definition_en: able to be seen, or easy to notice and recognise
core_image: 远处有个小点，越走越清楚，最后能认出是一个人
scene: 雾散了一点，山顶的塔终于从灰白里显出来。The far tower was not visible until the cloud lifted.
sceneCN: 这里 visible 是「看得见的」（第 1 个义项：能被眼睛看到）；句意为云散之前那座远处的塔看不见。由小点变成清晰人影的那段过程，就是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 看得见的；可见的；明显的

derivatives.zh: 加 -ly 构成，义为「明显地」
加 -ity 构成，义为「能见度；可见性」
加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「看不见的」
同根名词，义为「视力；愿景」

senses.title: Able to be seen by the eye
senses.definition: able to be seen, because light reaches it and then the eye
senses.definitionCN: 因有光到达并被眼睛接收而能被看到
senses.example: The far tower was not visible until the cloud lifted.
senses.exampleCN: 云散之前，那座远处的塔是看不见的。
senses.why: Latin videre, to see, gives the stem vis-, and -ible means able to be; visible is literally able to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 videre（看见）给出词干 vis-，-ible 表示「能被…的」，visible 字面上就是「能被看见的」。

senses.title: Easy to notice
senses.definition: clear enough to be noticed at once, though not necessarily seen by the eye
senses.definitionCN: 清楚到能被立即注意到，尽管不一定用眼去看
senses.example: There were visible signs of strain in his face.
senses.exampleCN: 他脸上有明显的疲惫迹象。
senses.why: What the eye can notice without effort becomes a general word for anything easy to detect.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛不费力就能注意到的东西，成了任何易被察觉之物的通用说法。

senses.title: Of light, within the range the eye can see
senses.definition: of radiation, having a wavelength the human eye responds to
senses.definitionCN: 指辐射的波长在人的眼睛能反应的范围内
senses.example: Visible light lies between the infrared and the ultraviolet.
senses.exampleCN: 可见光位于红外与紫外之间。
senses.why: Physics used the word for the narrow band of light that is literally able to be seen.
senses.whyCN: 物理学用这个词指那一段字面上能被看见的光。

senses.title: Open to public view
senses.titleCN: 公开可见的；可被查到的
senses.definition: of records or activity, able to be checked or seen by others
senses.definitionCN: 指记录或活动可被他人查看
senses.example: The accounts are visible to every member of the club.
senses.exampleCN: 账目对俱乐部每位成员都可见。
senses.why: A thing to be checked must first be seen, so records are described as visible to those allowed to look.
senses.whyCN: 要被核对的东西先得能被看见，于是记录被描述为对被允许查看者可见。

senses.title: Prominent in public life
senses.definition: noticed often by the public, as a role or a person
senses.definitionCN: 被公众频繁注意，如某个角色或人物
senses.example: She became a visible figure in the campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 她成了这场运动中的显眼人物。
senses.why: The metaphor of being on view gives the modern sense of public prominence.
senses.whyCN: 「摆在人眼前」这个比喻给出了现代的公众显眼义。

intro.en: Visible is Latin visibilis, able to be seen, from videre, to see.
intro.cn: visible 即拉丁语 visibilis（能被看见的），来自 videre（看见）。

items.en: Videre meant to see, and its stem vis- spread into many later words.
items.cn: videre 意为看见，其词干 vis- 进入许多后来的词。

items.en: Visibilis added the ending -ibilis, meaning able to be, to the stem.
items.cn: visibilis 在词干上加 -ibilis（能被…的）。

items.en: Old French visible carried the word to English in the middle ages.
items.cn: 古法语 visible 在中世纪把这个词带进英语。

items.en: English used it first of things seen by the eye and soon of things merely plain.
items.cn: 英语先用它指眼睛所见之物，很快又指只是明白清楚的事。

items.en: Physics and administration then gave it the senses of visible light and visible records.
items.cn: 物理学与行政事务随后添上「可见光」与「可查阅记录」两义。

note.en: The first group holds the see-root family, the second the adjectives for clear and for hidden.
note.cn: 第一组收「看」词根族，第二组收表示清楚与隐藏的形容词。

entries.definition: The adverb, meaning in a way that can be seen.
The noun for the quality of being visible.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可见性、能见度」。

entries.definition: The opposite adjective, unable to be seen.
entries.definitionCN: 反义形容词，义为「看不见的」。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to seeing.
entries.definitionCN: 同根形容词，义为「视觉的」。

entries.definition: Seeming true, or plainly seen.
So clear that it cannot be missed.
Clear from the evidence at hand.
entries.definitionCN: 由现有证据看得很清楚。

entries.definition: Kept out of sight, the opposite of visible.
entries.definitionCN: 藏起来不被看见，与 visible 相对。

normalIntro.en: Vis- (see) plus -ible (able to be): a short pattern shared with audible and sensible.
normalIntro.cn: vis-（看见）加 -ible（能被…的）：与 audible、sensible 同一套构造。

normal.en: Visible is vis- plus -ible, able to be seen.
normal.cn: visible 是 vis- 加 -ible，义为「能被看见的」。

normal.en: In- makes invisible; -ly makes visibly; -ity makes visibility.
normal.cn: in- 构成 invisible，-ly 构成 visibly，-ity 构成 visibility。

normal.en: Visible light is only a small band of the spectrum.
normal.cn: 可见光只是光谱中很窄的一段。

normal.en: Apparent and evident are close, but visible is about being seen first.
normal.cn: apparent 与 evident 相近，visible 更强调先能被看见。

normal.en: A visible sign is one you notice without being told.
normal.cn: visible sign 是不用别人说就能注意到的迹象。

abstract.en: See a tiny mark on the horizon become a tower.
abstract.cn: 想象地平线上一个小点变成一座塔。

abstract.en: Hear a fact stated so plainly that nobody can miss it.
abstract.cn: 听一件事说得太直白，谁都不会漏掉。

abstract.en: Picture a record book open on a table for anyone to read.
abstract.cn: 想象一本记录簿摊在桌上，谁都能读。

examples.en: The coast was visible from the top of the hill.
examples.cn: 从山顶能看见海岸。

examples.en: There were no visible marks on the wall.
examples.cn: 墙上没有可见的痕迹。

examples.en: The stain is barely visible in this light.
examples.cn: 在这种光线下那块污迹几乎看不见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为择伯」——为挑东西的伯父能一眼看见，因为东西摆在明处。

root: 拉丁语 videre（看见）→ visibilis（能被看见的）→ 古法语 visible → 英语 visible；同根词有 vision、visual、advise。

sensesIntro.en: To be seen by the eye spreads to being easy to notice, to light itself, to open records and to public prominence.
sensesIntro.cn: 「被眼睛看见」先扩到容易察觉、再到光本身、再到公开记录与公众显眼。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a distant mark becoming a tower.
core.cn: 核心意象：远处的小点变成一座塔。

branches.en: The eye branch: the tower hidden by cloud.
branches.cn: 眼睛分支：被云遮住的塔。

branches.en: The notice branch: visible strain on a face.
branches.cn: 察觉分支：脸上明显的疲惫。

branches.en: The light branch: between infrared and ultraviolet.
branches.cn: 光分支：红外与紫外之间。

branches.en: The records branch: accounts open to members.
branches.cn: 记录分支：对会员公开的账目。

branches.en: The prominence branch: a visible figure in a campaign.
branches.cn: 显眼分支：运动中引人注目的人物。

intro.en: Vis- means to see; -ible, -ly, -ity and in- make the rest of the family.
intro.cn: vis- 意为看见，-ible、-ly、-ity、in- 造出其余词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and visibilis are both recorded, so the root is secure.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 与 visibilis 均有记录，词根可靠。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根携带「看见」之义。

items.example: It also gives video and evident.
items.exampleCN: 它还生出 video 与 evident。
它构成 visible 与 audible。
